# UCP SESSION NOTE - POSITIVE SOCIAL INTERACTION

**Client:** Ava Lee D.
**Date of Service:** 11/29/2025
**Program Location:** Liverpool TEC
**Lead Therapist:** Lily Campbell
**Co-Facilitator:** Elijah James, M.A.

---

## POSITIVE SOCIAL ENGAGEMENT SESSION

Ava demonstrated exceptional social skills during structured group activity at 
Liverpool TEC from 10:00 AM to 11:30 AM.

**PEER INTERACTIONS:**
Ava engaged appropriately with peers Zoey and Liam during board game activity. 
Initiated 5 social interactions, including:
- Sharing game pieces with Zoey
- Inviting Liam to join activity
- Requesting turn-taking using functional communication strategies

**COMMUNICATION SUCCESSES:**
Following recommendations from Dr. Hill, Ava utilized total communication approach 
effectively. Verbally expressed wants/needs 13 times throughout session.

**STAFF INTERACTIONS:**
Responded positively to prompts from Lily Campbell and Elijah James. 
Built rapport through shared interest in activities. Accepted redirection appropriately when needed.

**GROUP ACTIVITY PARTICIPATION:**
Activity: Cooperative board game
Duration: 45 minutes
Peers present: Zoey, Liam
Adult supervision: 1:3 staff-to-client ratio

**PARENT FEEDBACK:**
Angela Lee attended pickup and reported Ava has 
been initiating play with siblings at home more frequently. Contact maintained via daily communication log.

**RECOMMENDATIONS:**
- Continue social skills group at Liverpool TEC
- Increase peer interaction opportunities during unstructured time
- Collaborate with Dr. Hill for social-emotional assessment

**Documentation:** Lily Campbell
**Date:** 11/29/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

10:25 AM - ANTECEDENT
Sebastian was participating in group activity when transition announcement was made

Sebastian responded to planned ignoring combined with blocking strategy.

10:43 AM - DE-ESCALATION ACHIEVED
Sebastian returned to baseline. Moved to quiet room for recovery.

**INJURIES/DAMAGE:**
Staff: Emily Ramirez sustained minor scratch on left forearm, no medical treatment required
Property: Game materials damaged, approximate cost $29
Client: No injuries sustained

**IMMEDIATE PARENT CONTACT:**
Michelle Price contacted at 315.458.5678.
Parent acknowledged incident and requested details of antecedent triggers.

Helen Price contacted at 315-460-4567.
Parent confirmed evening check-in call and discussed home consistency strategies.

**MEDICAL CONSULTATION:**
Nurse Matthew Washington, M.A. consulted. Visual assessment of minor staff injury completed. 
No client injuries noted. No medical intervention required.

**RESTRICTIVE INTERVENTIONS USED:**
- SCIP-R Blocking Pads: Yes (Duration: 9 minutes)
- Physical Restraint: No
- Seclusion: No
- PRN Medication: Not administered

**FUNCTIONAL BEHAVIOR ASSESSMENT UPDATE:**
Data suggests escape function related to transition from preferred activities. 
Recommend FBA review with Emily Ramirez scheduled for 
5/3/2026.

**PSYCHIATRIC CONSULTATION:**
Dr. Malpezzi notified via phone message. Appointment maintained for 
5/5/2026.

**NOTIFICATIONS COMPLETED:**

- BSP modification considered for transition protocols
- Staff debriefing completed
- Additional transition warnings for next 72 hours

**Report filed:** 11/02/2025

been initiating play with siblings at home more frequently. Contact maintained via daily communication log.

**RECOMMENDATIONS:**
- Continue social skills group at Cicero TEC
- Increase peer interaction opportunities during unstructured time
- Collaborate with Dr. Martin for social-emotional assessment

**Documentation:** Aubrey Lee
**Date:** 11/27/2025

# UCP SESSION NOTE - MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR

**Client:** Lucas Torres
**Incident Date:** 10/30/2025
**Incident Time:** 2:15 PM
**Location:** 88 Geiger ICF
**Staff Present:** Joseph Ramos

---

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
Lucas was engaged in art activity at 88 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Lucas exhibited Brief withdrawal characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 2 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff Joseph Ramos implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

Lucas responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
5 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
Lucas participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Lucas was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with James Torres at (315)520-5678. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by Joseph Ramos
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

**Next session:** 04/22/2026 at 88 Geiger ICF
**Provider check-in:** Dr. Walker on 5/1/26

**Report filed by:** Joseph Ramos
**Filed:** 10/30/2025

# UCP SESSION NOTE - MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR

**Client:** Jack Patel S.
**Incident Date:** 11/06/2025
**Incident Time:** 2:15 PM
**Location:** 96 Geiger ICF
**Staff Present:** Elijah Phillips

---

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
Jack was engaged in art activity at 96 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Jack exhibited Brief withdrawal characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 3 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff Elijah Phillips implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

Jack responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
6 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
Jack participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Jack was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with Kevin Patel at 315.475.2345. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by Elijah Phillips
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

**Next session:** 4/22/2026 at 96 Geiger ICF
**Provider check-in:** Luke Singh, M.A. on 5/1/26

**Report filed by:** Elijah Phillips
**Filed:** 11/06/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

# UCP SESSION NOTE - MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR

**Client:** Amelia Torres T.
**Incident Date:** 10/18/2025
**Incident Time:** 11:20 AM
**Location:** 95 Geiger ICF
**Staff Present:** Henry Ramirez, M.A.

---

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
Amelia was engaged in art activity at 95 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Amelia exhibited Brief withdrawal characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 2 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff Henry Ramirez, M.A. implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

Amelia responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
5 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
Amelia participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Amelia was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with Mark Torres at (315)476-2345. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by Henry Ramirez
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time

- Increase trial complexity for vocational skills
- Reduce prompting to gestural level only
- Incorporate generalization setting

# UCP POST-CRISIS RECOVERY SESSION NOTE

**Client:** Samuel Reed
**Recovery Session Date:** 11/16/2025
**Original Incident Date:** 4/18/2026
**Location:** 95 Geiger ICF
**Staff:** Chloe Gutierrez
**Clinical Supervisor:** Noah Roberts, Behavior Specialist II

---

## POST-CRISIS THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTION

**INCIDENT REFERENCE:**
Critical incident on 4/18/2026 at 95 Geiger ICF.
Incident Report ID: INC-2026-7785
Type: Physical aggression toward peer and staff, property destruction
Duration: Escalation 8 minutes, restraint 23 minutes

TIME SINCE INCIDENT: 48 hours

**CURRENT SESSION PURPOSE:**
1. Therapeutic processing of incident
2. Safety planning reinforcement
3. Skill rebuilding for emotion regulation
4. Relationship repair with staff and peers

**SESSION ACTIVITIES:**

**THERAPEUTIC PROCESSING:**
Samuel participated in cognitive-behavioral processing with Chloe Gutierrez.

Discussion topics:
- Event sequence understanding using visual timeline
- Emotional identification (anger, frustration, feeling out of control)
- Alternative response strategies (asking for break, using calm-down space)
- Safety understanding (why restraint was necessary)

Samuel's insight: Demonstrated good understanding of event sequence, identified trigger, 
recognized inappropriate choice and impact on others.

**SAFETY PLANNING:**
Reviewed and updated safety protocols with Samuel.

**NEW SAFETY MEASURES IMPLEMENTED:**
Following incident on 4/18/2026:
1. Individual activity schedule - Implemented 4/19/26
2. Enhanced visual supports for emotion regulation - Implemented 04/19/2026
3. Enhanced monitoring during peer activities (1:2 ratio)

**PARENT COLLABORATION:**
Joint session with Samuel Reed.

Parents contacted at 315.436.7890 to confirm session attendance.

Discussion points:
- Home-program consistency for emotion regulation strategies
- Warning sign recognition (escalating voice volume, body tension, pacing)
- De-escalation support at home (offering break space, reducing demands)
- Communication protocols between home and program

**STAFF RELATIONSHIP REPAIR:**
Samuel met individually with staff involved in incident.
Facilitated by: Noah Roberts, Behavior Specialist II

Process included: Samuel's verbal apology, staff reassurance of continued support, 
discussion of moving forward. Staff reported positive interaction quality.

**BEHAVIORAL SUPPORT PLAN UPDATES:**
Modified BSP implemented April 19, 2026 following comprehensive review.

Changes include:
- Enhanced antecedent strategies (increased warnings before transitions)
- Additional teaching of replacement behaviors (requesting break using visual card)
- Updated crisis protocols (specific de-escalation sequence)
- Modified reinforcement schedule

Review team:
- Sebastian Carter, M.A. (Behavior Specialist)
- Dr. Jenkins (Occupational Therapist)
- Dr. Gifford (Speech-Language Pathologist)
- Dr. Hughes (Nursing)
- Parents: Samuel Reed

**PSYCHIATRIC FOLLOW-UP:**
Emergency consultation with Dr. Turner on 4/19/2026.

Medication adjustments:
- Dosage adjustment made
- Continue current regimen with modifications

Next psychiatric appointment: 5/14/2026

**SKILL REBUILDING:**
Focus areas identified:
1. Emotion regulation and identification
2. Requesting breaks appropriately
3. Appropriate peer interactions

Teaching sessions scheduled:
- Daily emotion identification practice with Chloe Gutierrez
- Twice weekly skills practice
- Break request training as needed throughout day

**ENVIRONMENTAL MODIFICATIONS:**
Changes made at 95 Geiger ICF following incident:

Physical environment:
- Designated "calm corner" with visual supports (Completed 4/19/2026)
- Additional soft seating for de-escalation space

Schedule modifications:
- Individual time for preferred activities
- Structured peer activities with higher staff ratio for 1 week

**MONITORING PROTOCOL:**
Enhanced monitoring period: 11/16/2025 through 5/4/2026 (2 weeks)

Monitoring frequency: Hourly emotion check-ins using 5-point scale
Documentation: Electronic incident tracking system + daily narrative notes

**CHECK-IN SCHEDULE:**
Daily check-ins with rotating staff:
- Morning: 8:30 AM (baseline mood assessment)
- Midday: 12:00 PM (activity participation check)
- Afternoon: 3:00 PM (end-of-day processing)

**PARENT COMMUNICATION PLAN:**
Daily updates to Samuel Reed:
- Method: Phone call
- Time: 4:00 PM daily
- Contact: 315.436.7890

**PROGRESS INDICATORS:**

# UCP SESSION NOTE - MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR

**Client:** Gomez, Harper
**Incident Date:** 11/04/2025
**Incident Time:** 11:20 AM
**Location:** 96 Geiger ICF
**Staff Present:** Harper Hall

---

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
Harper was engaged in art activity at 96 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Harper exhibited Verbal refusal characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 2 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff Harper Hall implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

Harper responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
4 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
Harper participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Harper was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with Susan Gomez at (315) 492-5678. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by Harper Hall
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

**Next session:** April 22, 2026 at 96 Geiger ICF
**Provider check-in:** Dr. Aung on 5/03/2026

**Report filed by:** Harper Hall
**Filed:** 11/04/2025

---

- Reduce prompting to gestural level only
- Incorporate generalization setting

**Client:** S. Cooper
**Session Date:** 10/22/2025
**Locations Observed:** 95 Geiger ICF, Cicero TEC, Baldwinsville TEC
**Observing Staff:** John Watson, M.Ed.

---

## ENVIRONMENTAL TRIGGER DOCUMENTATION

**TRANSITION 1:** 95 Geiger ICF → Cicero TEC
Time: 10:15 AM
Trigger: Unexpected staff change (regular driver unavailable)
Client Response: Moderate anxiety, verbal questioning, increased pacing

Sofia demonstrated heightened anxiety when informed of transition from 
95 Geiger ICF to Cicero TEC with unfamiliar driver. 
Environmental factors noted:
- Different vehicle than typical transport
- Substitute staff member instead of usual John Watson, M.Ed.

**TRANSITION 2:** Cicero TEC → Baldwinsville TEC
Time: 1:30 PM
Trigger: Schedule modification due to building maintenance
Client Response: Mild agitation, requesting return to familiar setting

**SCHEDULE DISRUPTION ANALYSIS:**
Originally scheduled appointment with Dr. Gonzalez at Cicero TEC on 
April 15, 2026 was 
rescheduled to 05/03/2026 
due to provider illness. Sofia exhibited increased anxiety and repetitive questioning 
about appointment status.

**PARENT CONTACT:**
Anthony Cooper contacted at (315)479-2345 to discuss 
schedule sensitivity. Parent reported Sofia frequently references upcoming appointments 
at home and struggles with last-minute changes.

**SENSORY ENVIRONMENT ASSESSMENT:**
95 Geiger ICF: Familiar lighting, low noise level, preferred seating available
Cicero TEC: Moderate noise level, fluorescent lighting, multiple peer interactions
Baldwinsville TEC: High activity level, variable noise, open floor plan

Consultation with Dr. Mitchell scheduled for May 16, 2026 
to assess sensory processing needs and environmental accommodation recommendations.

**RECOMMENDATIONS:**
- Increase transition warnings from 5 minutes to 15 minutes advance notice
- Environmental modifications at Cicero TEC:
  * Provide noise-canceling headphones during high-activity periods
  * Designate quiet space for breaks
- Schedule consistency protocol - avoid changes within 48 hours when possible
- Provider coordination for appointment preparation with visual schedule

**FOLLOW-UP:**
Meeting with Anthony Cooper scheduled 
5/8/26 
to review environmental sensitivities.

Contact Dr. Mitchell at 315-507-4567 for sensory consultation.

**Documented by:** John Watson, M.Ed.
**Date:** 10/22/2025

**Teaching Method:** Discrete trial training with naturalistic teaching

preparation skills at Cicero TEC. Session began at 10:00 AM with

# UCP SESSION NOTE - MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR

**Client:** Michael Gomez G.
**Incident Date:** 10/24/2025
**Incident Time:** 11:20 AM
**Location:** 96 Geiger ICF
**Staff Present:** Mia Lopez, CCC-SLP

---

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
Michael was engaged in art activity at 96 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Michael exhibited Minor non-compliance characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 3 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff Mia Lopez, CCC-SLP implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

Michael responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
5 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
Michael participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Michael was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with Ashley Gomez at 315.519.9012. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by Mia Lopez
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

**Next session:** April 22, 2026 at 96 Geiger ICF
**Provider check-in:** Oliver Sanchez, M.S. on 4/29/2026

**Report filed by:** Mia Lopez, CCC-SLP
**Filed:** 10/24/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

# UCP SESSION NOTE - SKILL ACQUISITION

**Client:** Ava Reyes
**Date of Birth:** 9/3/7
**Session Date:** 11/06/2025
**Program:** Syracuse TEC
**Time:** 3:00 PM - 4:30 PM
**Behavior Specialist:** Abigail Ward

---

## SKILL ACQUISITION SESSION

**Target Skill:** Multi-step vocational task completion
**Teaching Method:** Discrete trial training with naturalistic teaching

**SESSION SUMMARY:**
Ava participated in 45 discrete trial training sessions focusing on lunch service 
preparation skills at Syracuse TEC. Session began at 3:00 PM with 
hand washing and apron donning.

**TRIAL DATA:**
- Trial block 1: 76% accuracy across 15 trials
- Trial block 2: 80% accuracy across 15 trials  
- Trial block 3: 88% accuracy across 15 trials
- Overall session accuracy: 78%

**PROMPTING HIERARCHY:**
Initial trials required full physical prompting, progressing to verbal prompting only by session end. 
Ava demonstrated improvement in response latency from 8.5 seconds to 3.2 seconds.

**VOCATIONAL INTEGRATION:**
Ava practiced food service skills during lunch preparation. Staff Levi Ross, Behavior Specialist supervised and reported successful completion of assigned tasks with minimal support.

**PARENT COLLABORATION:**
Contacted Kimberly Reyes at 315.455.5678 to discuss home practice strategies. 
Parent reported Ava has been practicing sorting tasks at home with good success.

**NEXT SESSION GOALS:**
- Increase trial complexity for vocational skills
- Reduce prompting to gestural level only
- Incorporate generalization setting

**Therapist:** Abigail Ward
**Date signed:** 11/06/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

# UCP SESSION NOTE - MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR

**Client:** Oliver Garcia
**Incident Date:** 10/12/2025
**Incident Time:** 11:20 AM
**Location:** 95 Geiger ICF
**Staff Present:** Benjamin Bailey

---

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
Oliver was engaged in art activity at 95 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Oliver exhibited Brief withdrawal characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 4 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff Benjamin Bailey implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

Oliver responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
5 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
Oliver participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Oliver was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with Rachel Garcia at (315) 434-7890. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by Benjamin Bailey
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

**Next session:** 4/22/2026 at 95 Geiger ICF
**Provider check-in:** Dr. Perry on 5/02/2026

**Report filed by:** Benjamin Bailey
**Filed:** 10/12/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

**Time:** 1:00 PM - 2:00 PM
**Behavior Specialist:** Evelyn Thomas

---

## SKILL ACQUISITION SESSION

**Target Skill:** Multi-step vocational task completion
**Teaching Method:** Discrete trial training with naturalistic teaching

**SESSION SUMMARY:**
Noah participated in 45 discrete trial training sessions focusing on lunch service 
preparation skills at Baldwinsville TEC. Session began at 1:00 PM with 
hand washing and apron donning.

**TRIAL DATA:**
- Trial block 1: 77% accuracy across 15 trials
- Trial block 2: 84% accuracy across 15 trials  
- Trial block 3: 89% accuracy across 15 trials
- Overall session accuracy: 89%

**PROMPTING HIERARCHY:**
Initial trials required full physical prompting, progressing to verbal prompting only by session end. 
Noah demonstrated improvement in response latency from 8.5 seconds to 3.2 seconds.

**VOCATIONAL INTEGRATION:**
Noah practiced food service skills during lunch preparation. Staff Zoey Robinson, Behavior Specialist I supervised and reported successful completion of assigned tasks with minimal support.

**PARENT COLLABORATION:**
Contacted Benjamin Lopez at (315) 446-7890 to discuss home practice strategies. 
Parent reported Noah has been practicing sorting tasks at home with good success.

**NEXT SESSION GOALS:**
- Increase trial complexity for vocational skills
- Reduce prompting to gestural level only
- Incorporate generalization setting

**Therapist:** Evelyn Thomas
**Date signed:** 11/12/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

Parent reported Samuel has been practicing sorting tasks at home with good success.

**NEXT SESSION GOALS:**
- Increase trial complexity for vocational skills
- Reduce prompting to gestural level only
- Incorporate generalization setting

**Therapist:** Noah Jimenez
**Date signed:** 10/05/2025

---

# UCP SESSION NOTE - MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR

**Client:** Turner, Abigail
**Incident Date:** 11/19/2025
**Incident Time:** 2:15 PM
**Location:** 96 Geiger ICF
**Staff Present:** David Phillips

---

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
Abigail was engaged in art activity at 96 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Abigail exhibited Brief withdrawal characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 5 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff David Phillips implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

Abigail responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
7 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
Abigail participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Abigail was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with William Turner at (315)464-5678. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by David Phillips
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

**Next session:** 4/22/2026 at 96 Geiger ICF
**Provider check-in:** Aria Carter, NP on May 4, 2026

**Report filed by:** David Phillips
**Filed:** 11/19/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

- Increase trial complexity for vocational skills
- Reduce prompting to gestural level only
- Incorporate generalization setting

**Therapist:** Owen Gutierrez

# UCP SESSION NOTE - MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR

**Client:** Jacob Thomas
**Incident Date:** 10/03/2025
**Incident Time:** 2:15 PM
**Location:** 92 Geiger ICF
**Staff Present:** William Jackson, BCBA, LBA

---

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
Jacob was engaged in art activity at 92 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Jacob exhibited Minor non-compliance characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 4 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff William Jackson, BCBA, LBA implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

Jacob responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
5 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
Jacob participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Jacob was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with Amanda Thomas at 315.512.5678. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by William Jackson
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

**Next session:** 04/22/2026 at 92 Geiger ICF
**Provider check-in:** Dr. Butler on 05/04/2026

**Report filed by:** William Jackson, BCBA, LBA
**Filed:** 10/03/2025

---

# UCP SESSION NOTE - MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR

**Client:** Ross, Benjamin
**Incident Date:** 10/23/2025
**Incident Time:** 2:15 PM
**Location:** 92 Geiger ICF
**Staff Present:** Chloe Rogers

---

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
Benjamin was engaged in art activity at 92 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Benjamin exhibited Brief withdrawal characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 4 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff Chloe Rogers implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

Benjamin responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
7 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
Benjamin participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Benjamin was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with William Ross at 315-512-5678. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by Chloe Rogers
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

**Next session:** 4/22/26 at 92 Geiger ICF
**Provider check-in:** Dr. Henderson on April 30, 2026

**Report filed by:** Chloe Rogers
**Filed:** 10/23/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

**Client:** Phillips, Sophia
**Incident Date:** 10/15/2025
**Incident Time:** 10:45 AM
**Location:** 88 Geiger ICF
**Staff Present:** Samuel Brooks

---

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
Sophia was engaged in art activity at 88 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Sophia exhibited Verbal refusal characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 5 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff Samuel Brooks implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

Sophia responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
6 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
Sophia participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Sophia was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with Nathan Phillips at (315) 431-8901. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by Samuel Brooks
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

**Next session:** 4/22/2026 at 88 Geiger ICF
**Provider check-in:** Dr. Russell on 4/30/2026

**Report filed by:** Samuel Brooks
**Filed:** 10/15/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

# UCP SESSION NOTE - MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR

**Client:** Ramirez, Noah
**Incident Date:** 10/05/2025
**Incident Time:** 11:20 AM
**Location:** 100 Geiger ICF
**Staff Present:** Lily Cox

---

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
Noah was engaged in art activity at 100 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Noah exhibited Brief withdrawal characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 5 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff Lily Cox implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

Noah responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
7 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
Noah participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Noah was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with Margaret Ramirez at 315.496.4567. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by Lily Cox
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

**Next session:** 4/22/2026 at 100 Geiger ICF
**Provider check-in:** Dr. Rodriguez on 5/5/2026

**Report filed by:** Lily Cox
**Filed:** 10/05/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

## POST-CRISIS THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTION

**INCIDENT REFERENCE:**
Critical incident on 4/18/26 at 95 Geiger ICF.
Incident Report ID: INC-2026-4674
Type: Physical aggression toward peer and staff, property destruction
Duration: Escalation 5 minutes, restraint 19 minutes

TIME SINCE INCIDENT: 48 hours

**CURRENT SESSION PURPOSE:**
1. Therapeutic processing of incident
2. Safety planning reinforcement
3. Skill rebuilding for emotion regulation
4. Relationship repair with staff and peers

**SESSION ACTIVITIES:**

**THERAPEUTIC PROCESSING:**
Lucas participated in cognitive-behavioral processing with Mason Morris.

Discussion topics:
- Event sequence understanding using visual timeline
- Emotional identification (anger, frustration, feeling out of control)
- Alternative response strategies (asking for break, using calm-down space)
- Safety understanding (why restraint was necessary)

Lucas's insight: Demonstrated good understanding of event sequence, identified trigger, 
recognized inappropriate choice and impact on others.

**SAFETY PLANNING:**
Reviewed and updated safety protocols with Lucas.

**NEW SAFETY MEASURES IMPLEMENTED:**
Following incident on 4/18/26:
1. Individual activity schedule - Implemented April 19, 2026
2. Enhanced visual supports for emotion regulation - Implemented 04/19/2026
3. Enhanced monitoring during peer activities (1:2 ratio)

**PARENT COLLABORATION:**
Joint session with William Murphy.

Parents contacted at (315)463-2345 to confirm session attendance.

Discussion points:
- Home-program consistency for emotion regulation strategies
- Warning sign recognition (escalating voice volume, body tension, pacing)
- De-escalation support at home (offering break space, reducing demands)
- Communication protocols between home and program

**STAFF RELATIONSHIP REPAIR:**
Lucas met individually with staff involved in incident.
Facilitated by: Harper Phillips, NP

Process included: Lucas's verbal apology, staff reassurance of continued support, 
discussion of moving forward. Staff reported positive interaction quality.

**BEHAVIORAL SUPPORT PLAN UPDATES:**
Modified BSP implemented 4/19/2026 following comprehensive review.

Changes include:
- Enhanced antecedent strategies (increased warnings before transitions)
- Additional teaching of replacement behaviors (requesting break using visual card)
- Updated crisis protocols (specific de-escalation sequence)
- Modified reinforcement schedule

Review team:
- Ella Roberts, NP (Behavior Specialist)
- Dr. Kim (Occupational Therapist)
- Dr. Raju (Speech-Language Pathologist)
- Dr. Alexander (Nursing)
- Parents: William Murphy

Emergency consultation with Dr. Ward on 4/19/2026.

Medication adjustments:
- Increased evening anxiety medication
- Continue current regimen with modifications

Next psychiatric appointment: 5/13/2026

**SKILL REBUILDING:**
Focus areas identified:
1. Emotion regulation and identification
2. Requesting breaks appropriately
3. Appropriate peer interactions

Teaching sessions scheduled:
- Daily emotion identification practice with Mason Morris
- Twice weekly skills practice
- Break request training as needed throughout day

**ENVIRONMENTAL MODIFICATIONS:**
Changes made at 95 Geiger ICF following incident:

Physical environment:
- Designated "calm corner" with visual supports (Completed April 19, 2026)
- Additional soft seating for de-escalation space

Schedule modifications:
- Individual time for preferred activities
- Structured peer activities with higher staff ratio for 1 week

**MONITORING PROTOCOL:**
Enhanced monitoring period: 11/22/2025 through 5/4/26 (2 weeks)

Monitoring frequency: Hourly emotion check-ins using 5-point scale
Documentation: Electronic incident tracking system + daily narrative notes

**CHECK-IN SCHEDULE:**
Daily check-ins with rotating staff:
- Morning: 8:30 AM (baseline mood assessment)
- Midday: 12:00 PM (activity participation check)
- Afternoon: 3:00 PM (end-of-day processing)

Daily updates to William Murphy:
- Method: Phone call

- Contact: (315)463-2345

- Zero physical aggression incidents
- Appropriate use of break request card 3 times
- Positive peer interactions during structured activities (100% appropriate)
- Verbal communication of emotions using 5-point scale with 76% accuracy

been initiating play with siblings at home more frequently. Contact maintained via daily communication log.

**RECOMMENDATIONS:**
- Continue social skills group at Cicero TEC
- Increase peer interaction opportunities during unstructured time
- Collaborate with Ethan Murphy, LCSW for social-emotional assessment

**Documentation:** Grace Foster

**Observing Staff:** Charlotte Turner

## ENVIRONMENTAL TRIGGER DOCUMENTATION

**TRANSITION 1:** 95 Geiger ICF → Cicero TEC
Time: 9:30 AM
Trigger: Unexpected staff change (regular driver unavailable)
Client Response: Moderate anxiety, verbal questioning, increased pacing

Grace demonstrated heightened anxiety when informed of transition from 
95 Geiger ICF to Cicero TEC with unfamiliar driver. 
Environmental factors noted:
- Different vehicle than typical transport
- Substitute staff member instead of usual Charlotte Turner

**TRANSITION 2:** Cicero TEC → Syracuse TEC
Time: 2:15 PM

Client Response: Mild agitation, requesting return to familiar setting

Originally scheduled appointment with Dr. Martinez at Cicero TEC on 
04/12/2026 was 
rescheduled to 05/03/2026 
due to provider illness. Grace exhibited increased anxiety and repetitive questioning 
about appointment status.

**PARENT CONTACT:**
Jason Hughes contacted at (315) 503-9012 to discuss 
schedule sensitivity. Parent reported Grace frequently references upcoming appointments 
at home and struggles with last-minute changes.

**SENSORY ENVIRONMENT ASSESSMENT:**
95 Geiger ICF: Familiar lighting, low noise level, preferred seating available
Cicero TEC: Moderate noise level, fluorescent lighting, multiple peer interactions
Syracuse TEC: High activity level, variable noise, open floor plan

Consultation with Benjamin Singh, BCBA scheduled for May 27, 2026 
to assess sensory processing needs and environmental accommodation recommendations.

**RECOMMENDATIONS:**
- Increase transition warnings from 5 minutes to 15 minutes advance notice
- Environmental modifications at Cicero TEC:
  * Provide noise-canceling headphones during high-activity periods
  * Designate quiet space for breaks
- Schedule consistency protocol - avoid changes within 48 hours when possible
- Provider coordination for appointment preparation with visual schedule

**FOLLOW-UP:**
Meeting with Jason Hughes scheduled 
05/03/2026 
to review environmental sensitivities.

Contact Benjamin Singh, BCBA at 315-425-8901 for sensory consultation.

**Documented by:** Charlotte Turner
**Date:** 10/16/2025

Reviewed and updated safety protocols with Evelyn.

**Client:** Olivia Campbell
**Recovery Session Date:** 10/27/2025
**Original Incident Date:** 4/18/26
**Location:** 95 Geiger ICF
**Staff:** Victoria Gomez
**Clinical Supervisor:** Emma Ward, BCBA, BCBA, LBA

---

## POST-CRISIS THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTION

**INCIDENT REFERENCE:**
Critical incident on 4/18/26 at 95 Geiger ICF.
Incident Report ID: INC-2026-5161
Type: Physical aggression toward peer and staff, property destruction
Duration: Escalation 5 minutes, restraint 21 minutes

TIME SINCE INCIDENT: 48 hours

**CURRENT SESSION PURPOSE:**
1. Therapeutic processing of incident
2. Safety planning reinforcement
3. Skill rebuilding for emotion regulation
4. Relationship repair with staff and peers

**SESSION ACTIVITIES:**

**THERAPEUTIC PROCESSING:**
Olivia participated in cognitive-behavioral processing with Victoria Gomez.

Discussion topics:
- Event sequence understanding using visual timeline
- Emotional identification (anger, frustration, feeling out of control)
- Alternative response strategies (asking for break, using calm-down space)
- Safety understanding (why restraint was necessary)

Olivia's insight: Demonstrated good understanding of event sequence, identified trigger, 
recognized inappropriate choice and impact on others.

**SAFETY PLANNING:**
Reviewed and updated safety protocols with Olivia.

**NEW SAFETY MEASURES IMPLEMENTED:**
Following incident on 4/18/26:
1. Individual activity schedule - Implemented 04/19/2026
2. Enhanced visual supports for emotion regulation - Implemented 04/19/2026
3. Enhanced monitoring during peer activities (1:2 ratio)

**PARENT COLLABORATION:**
Joint session with Michael Campbell and Barbara Campbell.

Parents contacted at (315)520-5678 to confirm session attendance.

Discussion points:
- Home-program consistency for emotion regulation strategies
- Warning sign recognition (escalating voice volume, body tension, pacing)
- De-escalation support at home (offering break space, reducing demands)
- Communication protocols between home and program

**STAFF RELATIONSHIP REPAIR:**
Olivia met individually with staff involved in incident.
Facilitated by: Emma Ward, BCBA, BCBA, LBA

Process included: Olivia's verbal apology, staff reassurance of continued support, 
discussion of moving forward. Staff reported positive interaction quality.

**BEHAVIORAL SUPPORT PLAN UPDATES:**
Modified BSP implemented 4/19/2026 following comprehensive review.

Changes include:
- Enhanced antecedent strategies (increased warnings before transitions)
- Additional teaching of replacement behaviors (requesting break using visual card)
- Updated crisis protocols (specific de-escalation sequence)
- Modified reinforcement schedule

Review team:
- Aria King, Psy.D. (Behavior Specialist)
- Dr. King (Occupational Therapist)
- Dr. Torres (Speech-Language Pathologist)
- Dr. Pollard (Nursing)
- Parents: Michael Campbell, Barbara Campbell

**PSYCHIATRIC FOLLOW-UP:**
Emergency consultation with Dr. Bennett on 4/19/26.

Medication adjustments:
- Dosage adjustment made
- Continue current regimen with modifications

Next psychiatric appointment: 5/24/2026

**SKILL REBUILDING:**
Focus areas identified:
1. Emotion regulation and identification
2. Requesting breaks appropriately
3. Appropriate peer interactions

Teaching sessions scheduled:
- Daily emotion identification practice with Victoria Gomez
- Twice weekly skills practice
- Break request training as needed throughout day

**ENVIRONMENTAL MODIFICATIONS:**
Changes made at 95 Geiger ICF following incident:

Physical environment:
- Designated "calm corner" with visual supports (Completed 04/19/2026)
- Additional soft seating for de-escalation space

Schedule modifications:
- Individual time for preferred activities
- Structured peer activities with higher staff ratio for 1 week

**MONITORING PROTOCOL:**
Enhanced monitoring period: 10/27/2025 through 5/04/2026 (2 weeks)

Monitoring frequency: Hourly emotion check-ins using 5-point scale
Documentation: Electronic incident tracking system + daily narrative notes

**CHECK-IN SCHEDULE:**
Daily check-ins with rotating staff:
- Morning: 8:30 AM (baseline mood assessment)
- Midday: 12:00 PM (activity participation check)
- Afternoon: 3:00 PM (end-of-day processing)

**PARENT COMMUNICATION PLAN:**
Daily updates to Michael Campbell:
- Method: Phone call
- Time: 4:00 PM daily
- Contact: (315)520-5678

**PROGRESS INDICATORS:**
Since incident on 4/18/26 (48 hours post-incident):
- Zero physical aggression incidents
- Appropriate use of break request card 2 times
- Positive peer interactions during structured activities (100% appropriate)
- Verbal communication of emotions using 5-point scale with 75% accuracy

**NEXT STEPS:**
☑ Continue daily monitoring through 5/4/26
☑ BSP implementation fidelity checks (daily by supervisor)
☑ Ongoing parent collaboration (daily calls)
☑ Psychiatric follow-up 5/25/2026
☑ Incident review team meeting scheduled
☑ FBA update completion target: 04/29/2026

**DOCUMENTATION:**
Recovery session documented by: Victoria Gomez
Clinical supervision: Emma Ward, BCBA, BCBA, LBA
Parent consent obtained: 10/27/2025
Treatment plan updated: April 19, 2026

Session date: 10/27/2025
Next recovery session: 4/27/2026

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
James was engaged in art activity at 88 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
James exhibited Verbal refusal characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 2 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff Lucas Sanders implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

James responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
6 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
James participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
James was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with Brandon Moore at (315) 470-1234. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by Lucas Sanders
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

**Next session:** 04/22/2026 at 88 Geiger ICF

**Client:** Thomas, Luke
**Recovery Session Date:** 10/23/2025
**Original Incident Date:** 4/18/2026
**Location:** 88 Geiger ICF
**Staff:** Mia Ward
**Clinical Supervisor:** Ella Davis, Psy.D.

---

## POST-CRISIS THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTION

**INCIDENT REFERENCE:**
Critical incident on 4/18/2026 at 88 Geiger ICF.
Incident Report ID: INC-2026-3414
Type: Physical aggression toward peer and staff, property destruction
Duration: Escalation 5 minutes, restraint 24 minutes

TIME SINCE INCIDENT: 48 hours

**CURRENT SESSION PURPOSE:**
1. Therapeutic processing of incident
2. Safety planning reinforcement
3. Skill rebuilding for emotion regulation
4. Relationship repair with staff and peers

**SESSION ACTIVITIES:**

**THERAPEUTIC PROCESSING:**
Luke participated in cognitive-behavioral processing with Mia Ward.

Discussion topics:
- Event sequence understanding using visual timeline
- Emotional identification (anger, frustration, feeling out of control)
- Alternative response strategies (asking for break, using calm-down space)
- Safety understanding (why restraint was necessary)

Luke's insight: Demonstrated good understanding of event sequence, identified trigger, 
recognized inappropriate choice and impact on others.

**SAFETY PLANNING:**
Reviewed and updated safety protocols with Luke.

**NEW SAFETY MEASURES IMPLEMENTED:**
Following incident on 4/18/2026:
1. Individual activity schedule - Implemented April 19, 2026
2. Enhanced visual supports for emotion regulation - Implemented April 19, 2026
3. Enhanced monitoring during peer activities (1:2 ratio)

**PARENT COLLABORATION:**
Joint session with Jacob Thomas and Angela Thomas.

Parents contacted at (315)480-7890 to confirm session attendance.

Discussion points:
- Home-program consistency for emotion regulation strategies
- Warning sign recognition (escalating voice volume, body tension, pacing)
- De-escalation support at home (offering break space, reducing demands)
- Communication protocols between home and program

**STAFF RELATIONSHIP REPAIR:**
Luke met individually with staff involved in incident.
Facilitated by: Ella Davis, Psy.D.

Process included: Luke's verbal apology, staff reassurance of continued support, 
discussion of moving forward. Staff reported positive interaction quality.

**BEHAVIORAL SUPPORT PLAN UPDATES:**
Modified BSP implemented 4/19/2026 following comprehensive review.

Changes include:
- Enhanced antecedent strategies (increased warnings before transitions)
- Additional teaching of replacement behaviors (requesting break using visual card)
- Updated crisis protocols (specific de-escalation sequence)
- Modified reinforcement schedule

Review team:
- Logan Watson, Behavior Specialist II, M.A. (Behavior Specialist)
- Dr. Moore (Occupational Therapist)
- Dr. Nguyen (Speech-Language Pathologist)
- Olivia Patterson, Ph.D. (Nursing)
- Parents: Jacob Thomas, Angela Thomas

**PSYCHIATRIC FOLLOW-UP:**
Emergency consultation with Dr. Rivera on 04/19/2026.

Medication adjustments:
- Added PRN protocol
- Continue current regimen with modifications

Next psychiatric appointment: 05/14/2026

**SKILL REBUILDING:**
Focus areas identified:
1. Emotion regulation and identification
2. Requesting breaks appropriately
3. Appropriate peer interactions

Teaching sessions scheduled:
- Daily emotion identification practice with Mia Ward
- Twice weekly skills practice
- Break request training as needed throughout day

**ENVIRONMENTAL MODIFICATIONS:**
Changes made at 88 Geiger ICF following incident:

Physical environment:
- Designated "calm corner" with visual supports (Completed 4/19/2026)
- Additional soft seating for de-escalation space

Schedule modifications:
- Individual time for preferred activities
- Structured peer activities with higher staff ratio for 1 week

**MONITORING PROTOCOL:**
Enhanced monitoring period: 10/23/2025 through 5/4/26 (2 weeks)

Monitoring frequency: Hourly emotion check-ins using 5-point scale
Documentation: Electronic incident tracking system + daily narrative notes

**CHECK-IN SCHEDULE:**
Daily check-ins with rotating staff:
- Morning: 8:30 AM (baseline mood assessment)
- Midday: 12:00 PM (activity participation check)
- Afternoon: 3:00 PM (end-of-day processing)

**PARENT COMMUNICATION PLAN:**
Daily updates to Jacob Thomas:
- Method: Phone call
- Time: 4:00 PM daily
- Contact: (315)480-7890

**PROGRESS INDICATORS:**
Since incident on 4/18/2026 (48 hours post-incident):
- Zero physical aggression incidents
- Appropriate use of break request card 3 times
- Positive peer interactions during structured activities (100% appropriate)
- Verbal communication of emotions using 5-point scale with 84% accuracy

**NEXT STEPS:**
☑ Continue daily monitoring through 5/04/2026
☑ BSP implementation fidelity checks (daily by supervisor)
☑ Ongoing parent collaboration (daily calls)
☑ Psychiatric follow-up 05/13/2026
☑ Incident review team meeting scheduled
☑ FBA update completion target: 4/30/26

**DOCUMENTATION:**

Clinical supervision: Ella Davis, Psy.D.

Treatment plan updated: 04/19/2026

**Teaching Method:** Discrete trial training with naturalistic teaching

preparation skills at Liverpool TEC. Session began at 2:00 PM with 
hand washing and apron donning.

Liam practiced food service skills during lunch preparation. Staff Aubrey Williams, LMFT supervised and reported successful completion of assigned tasks with minimal support.

**PARENT COLLABORATION:**
Contacted Maria White at 315.506.8901 to discuss home practice strategies. 
Parent reported Liam has been practicing sorting tasks at home with good success.

**NEXT SESSION GOALS:**
- Increase trial complexity for vocational skills
- Reduce prompting to gestural level only
- Incorporate generalization setting

**Therapist:** Owen Morgan
**Date signed:** 11/14/2025

END OF SESSION NOTE

**TRANSITION 1:** 88 Geiger ICF → Cicero TEC

- Substitute staff member instead of usual Luke Turner

due to provider illness. Oliver exhibited increased anxiety and repetitive questioning 
about appointment status.

**PARENT CONTACT:**
Aaron Rodriguez contacted at (315) 425-8901 to discuss 
schedule sensitivity. Parent reported Oliver frequently references upcoming appointments 
at home and struggles with last-minute changes.

**SENSORY ENVIRONMENT ASSESSMENT:**
88 Geiger ICF: Familiar lighting, low noise level, preferred seating available
Cicero TEC: Moderate noise level, fluorescent lighting, multiple peer interactions
Syracuse TEC: High activity level, variable noise, open floor plan

Consultation with Elijah Baker, CNS scheduled for 5/27/2026 
to assess sensory processing needs and environmental accommodation recommendations.

- Increase transition warnings from 5 minutes to 15 minutes advance notice

  * Designate quiet space for breaks

- Provider coordination for appointment preparation with visual schedule

**FOLLOW-UP:**

to review environmental sensitivities.

**ANTECEDENT:**
David was engaged in art activity at 88 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
David exhibited Minor non-compliance characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 2 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff David Allen, M.A. implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

David responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
7 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
David participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
David was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with Carolyn Martinez at (315) 454-4567. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by David Allen
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

# UCP SESSION NOTE - MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR

**Client:** A. James
**Incident Date:** 10/20/2025
**Incident Time:** 11:20 AM
**Location:** 100 Geiger ICF
**Staff Present:** Lily Brooks

---

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
Amelia was engaged in art activity at 100 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Amelia exhibited Brief withdrawal characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 2 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff Lily Brooks implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

Amelia responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
7 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
Amelia participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Amelia was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with Jennifer James at 315.500.1234. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by Lily Brooks
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

**Next session:** 4/22/26 at 100 Geiger ICF
**Provider check-in:** John Richardson, OTR/L on 4/28/2026

**Report filed by:** Lily Brooks
**Filed:** 10/20/2025

---

about appointment status.

at home and struggles with last-minute changes.

  * Designate quiet space for breaks
- Schedule consistency protocol - avoid changes within 48 hours when possible

# UCP SESSION NOTE - MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR

**Client:** Elijah Roberts K.
**Incident Date:** 10/23/2025
**Incident Time:** 11:20 AM
**Location:** 96 Geiger ICF
**Staff Present:** Owen Jones

---

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
Elijah was engaged in art activity at 96 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Elijah exhibited Brief withdrawal characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 3 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff Owen Jones implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

Elijah responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
5 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
Elijah participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Elijah was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with James Roberts at (315)472-5678. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by Owen Jones
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

**Next session:** 4/22/26 at 96 Geiger ICF
**Provider check-in:** Samuel Scott, Psy.D. on May 3, 2026

**Report filed by:** Owen Jones
**Filed:** 10/23/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

# UCP SESSION NOTE - ENVIRONMENTAL TRIGGER ANALYSIS

**Client:** Harris, Aiden P.
**Session Date:** 11/07/2025
**Locations Observed:** 88 Geiger ICF, Cicero TEC, Chadwicks TEC
**Observing Staff:** Mia Murphy

---

## ENVIRONMENTAL TRIGGER DOCUMENTATION

**TRANSITION 1:** 88 Geiger ICF → Cicero TEC
Time: 8:45 AM
Trigger: Unexpected staff change (regular driver unavailable)
Client Response: Moderate anxiety, verbal questioning, increased pacing

Aiden demonstrated heightened anxiety when informed of transition from 
88 Geiger ICF to Cicero TEC with unfamiliar driver. 
Environmental factors noted:
- Different vehicle than typical transport
- Substitute staff member instead of usual Mia Murphy

**TRANSITION 2:** Cicero TEC → Chadwicks TEC
Time: 2:15 PM
Trigger: Schedule modification due to building maintenance
Client Response: Mild agitation, requesting return to familiar setting

**SCHEDULE DISRUPTION ANALYSIS:**
Originally scheduled appointment with Dr. Simmons at Cicero TEC on 
4/13/26 was 
rescheduled to 05/04/2026 
due to provider illness. Aiden exhibited increased anxiety and repetitive questioning 
about appointment status.

**PARENT CONTACT:**
David Harris contacted at (315) 440-7890 to discuss 
schedule sensitivity. Parent reported Aiden frequently references upcoming appointments 
at home and struggles with last-minute changes.

**SENSORY ENVIRONMENT ASSESSMENT:**
88 Geiger ICF: Familiar lighting, low noise level, preferred seating available
Cicero TEC: Moderate noise level, fluorescent lighting, multiple peer interactions
Chadwicks TEC: High activity level, variable noise, open floor plan

Consultation with Dr. Gonzales scheduled for 5/15/2026 
to assess sensory processing needs and environmental accommodation recommendations.

**RECOMMENDATIONS:**
- Increase transition warnings from 5 minutes to 15 minutes advance notice
- Environmental modifications at Cicero TEC:
  * Provide noise-canceling headphones during high-activity periods
  * Designate quiet space for breaks
- Schedule consistency protocol - avoid changes within 48 hours when possible

- Incorporate generalization setting

effectively. Verbally expressed wants/needs 14 times throughout session.

Responded positively to prompts from Harper Phillips and Avery Morgan.

**GROUP ACTIVITY PARTICIPATION:**
Activity: Cooperative board game

Peers present: Chloe, Charlotte
Adult supervision: 1:3 staff-to-client ratio

**PARENT FEEDBACK:**
Laura Adams attended pickup and reported Sophia has 
been initiating play with siblings at home more frequently. Contact maintained via daily communication log.

**RECOMMENDATIONS:**
- Continue social skills group at Chadwicks TEC
- Increase peer interaction opportunities during unstructured time
- Collaborate with Dr. Scott for social-emotional assessment

**Documentation:** Harper Phillips, CCC-SLP
**Date:** 11/12/2025

# UCP SESSION NOTE - MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR

**Client:** Matthew Ross
**Incident Date:** 11/11/2025
**Incident Time:** 2:15 PM
**Location:** 88 Geiger ICF
**Staff Present:** Lucas Hernandez

---

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
Matthew was engaged in art activity at 88 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Matthew exhibited Brief withdrawal characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 4 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff Lucas Hernandez implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

Matthew responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
6 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
Matthew participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Matthew was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with Brandon Ross at 315.485.2345. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by Lucas Hernandez
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

**Next session:** 4/22/2026 at 88 Geiger ICF
**Provider check-in:** Luke Howard, MS, CCC-SLP on 5/1/26

**Report filed by:** Lucas Hernandez
**Filed:** 11/11/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

- Increase trial complexity for vocational skills
- Reduce prompting to gestural level only
- Incorporate generalization setting

# UCP SESSION NOTE - MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR

**Client:** Sophia Bailey
**Incident Date:** 11/07/2025
**Incident Time:** 10:45 AM
**Location:** 96 Geiger ICF
**Staff Present:** Abigail Hughes, M.A.

---

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
Sophia was engaged in art activity at 96 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Sophia exhibited Brief withdrawal characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 2 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff Abigail Hughes, M.A. implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

Sophia responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
6 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
Sophia participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Sophia was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with Nicholas Bailey at 315-442-9012. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by Abigail Hughes
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

**Next session:** April 22, 2026 at 96 Geiger ICF
**Provider check-in:** James Parker, NP on 5/5/2026

**Report filed by:** Abigail Hughes, M.A.
**Filed:** 11/07/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

**Observing Staff:** William Gomez, PhD, BCBA

---

## ENVIRONMENTAL TRIGGER DOCUMENTATION

**TRANSITION 1:** 92 Geiger ICF → Baldwinsville TEC
Time: 10:15 AM
Trigger: Unexpected staff change (regular driver unavailable)
Client Response: Moderate anxiety, verbal questioning, increased pacing

Lily demonstrated heightened anxiety when informed of transition from 
92 Geiger ICF to Baldwinsville TEC with unfamiliar driver. 
Environmental factors noted:
- Different vehicle than typical transport
- Substitute staff member instead of usual William Gomez, PhD, BCBA

**TRANSITION 2:** Baldwinsville TEC → Syracuse TEC
Time: 1:30 PM
Trigger: Schedule modification due to building maintenance
Client Response: Mild agitation, requesting return to familiar setting

Originally scheduled appointment with Dr. Cox at Baldwinsville TEC on 
4/12/26 was 
rescheduled to 4/29/2026 
due to provider illness. Lily exhibited increased anxiety and repetitive questioning 
about appointment status.

**PARENT CONTACT:**
Nancy Williams contacted at (315) 478-9012 to discuss 
schedule sensitivity. Parent reported Lily frequently references upcoming appointments 
at home and struggles with last-minute changes.

**SENSORY ENVIRONMENT ASSESSMENT:**
92 Geiger ICF: Familiar lighting, low noise level, preferred seating available
Baldwinsville TEC: Moderate noise level, fluorescent lighting, multiple peer interactions
Syracuse TEC: High activity level, variable noise, open floor plan

Consultation with Dr. Brooks scheduled for 5/20/26 
to assess sensory processing needs and environmental accommodation recommendations.

**RECOMMENDATIONS:**
- Increase transition warnings from 5 minutes to 15 minutes advance notice
- Environmental modifications at Baldwinsville TEC:
  * Provide noise-canceling headphones during high-activity periods
  * Designate quiet space for breaks
- Schedule consistency protocol - avoid changes within 48 hours when possible
- Provider coordination for appointment preparation with visual schedule

**FOLLOW-UP:**
Meeting with Nancy Williams scheduled 
5/3/26 
to review environmental sensitivities.

Contact Dr. Brooks at 315-487-9012 for sensory consultation.

**Documented by:** William Gomez, PhD, BCBA
**Date:** 11/13/2025

# UCP SESSION NOTE - MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR

**Client:** Hill, Lucas
**Incident Date:** 11/29/2025
**Incident Time:** 11:20 AM
**Location:** 96 Geiger ICF
**Staff Present:** Henry Ramos

---

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
Lucas was engaged in art activity at 96 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Lucas exhibited Brief withdrawal characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 2 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff Henry Ramos implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

Lucas responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
5 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
Lucas participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Lucas was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with Jason Hill at 315.426.7890. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by Henry Ramos
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

**Next session:** April 22, 2026 at 96 Geiger ICF
**Provider check-in:** Aria Rivera, Ed.M. on 5/5/26

**Report filed by:** Henry Ramos
**Filed:** 11/29/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

# UCP SESSION NOTE - MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR

**Client:** Riley Allen
**Incident Date:** 11/19/2025
**Incident Time:** 11:20 AM
**Location:** 88 Geiger ICF
**Staff Present:** Luke Hughes

---

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
Riley was engaged in art activity at 88 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Riley exhibited Verbal refusal characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 5 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff Luke Hughes implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

Riley responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
5 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
Riley participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Riley was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with Justin Allen at 315.482.2345. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by Luke Hughes
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

**Next session:** 4/22/2026 at 88 Geiger ICF
**Provider check-in:** Dr. Watson on 05/02/2026

**Report filed by:** Luke Hughes
**Filed:** 11/19/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

# UCP SESSION NOTE - MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR

**Client:** William Wood
**Incident Date:** 10/10/2025
**Incident Time:** 11:20 AM
**Location:** 92 Geiger ICF
**Staff Present:** Julian Hernandez, M.Ed.

---

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
William was engaged in art activity at 92 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
William exhibited Verbal refusal characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 3 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff Julian Hernandez, M.Ed. implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

William responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
6 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
William participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
William was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with Kathleen Wood at 315-477-5678. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by Julian Hernandez
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

**Next session:** 4/22/2026 at 92 Geiger ICF
**Provider check-in:** Dr. Campbell on 4/30/26

**Report filed by:** Julian Hernandez, M.Ed.
**Filed:** 10/10/2025

- Increase trial complexity for vocational skills
- Reduce prompting to gestural level only
- Incorporate generalization setting

# UCP SESSION NOTE - MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR

**Client:** Sophia Ramos
**Incident Date:** 10/11/2025
**Incident Time:** 2:15 PM
**Location:** 95 Geiger ICF
**Staff Present:** Noah Nguyen

---

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
Sophia was engaged in art activity at 95 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Sophia exhibited Brief withdrawal characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 3 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff Noah Nguyen implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

Sophia responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
5 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
Sophia participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Sophia was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with Andrew Ramos at (315) 433-8901. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by Noah Nguyen
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

**Next session:** 4/22/26 at 95 Geiger ICF
**Provider check-in:** Dr. Gray on 5/4/26

**Report filed by:** Noah Nguyen
**Filed:** 10/11/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

- Increase trial complexity for vocational skills
- Reduce prompting to gestural level only
- Incorporate generalization setting

Charlotte was engaged in art activity at 96 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
