7 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
Charlotte participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Charlotte was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with Linda Mitchell at (315)478-9012. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

- Continue monitoring for pattern development

- Continue social skills group at Liverpool TEC

- Collaborate with Dr. Poissant for social-emotional assessment

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
Wyatt was engaged in art activity at 95 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Wyatt exhibited Minor non-compliance characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 2 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff Scarlett Jimenez implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

Wyatt responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
7 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
Wyatt participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Wyatt was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with Catherine Murphy at (315) 474-3456. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by Scarlett Jimenez
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

**NEXT SESSION GOALS:**
- Increase trial complexity for vocational skills
- Reduce prompting to gestural level only
- Incorporate generalization setting

**Client:** Mia Chavez
**Incident Date:** 10/22/2025
**Incident Time:** 10:45 AM
**Location:** 92 Geiger ICF
**Staff Present:** Grace James

---

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
Mia was engaged in art activity at 92 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Mia exhibited Brief withdrawal characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 2 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff Grace James implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

Mia responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
7 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
Mia participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Mia was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with Emily Chavez at (315)487-9012. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by Grace James
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

**Next session:** 4/22/2026 at 92 Geiger ICF
**Provider check-in:** Olivia Aung, Ph.D. on 05/05/2026

**Report filed by:** Grace James
**Filed:** 10/22/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

# UCP SESSION NOTE - ENVIRONMENTAL TRIGGER ANALYSIS

**Client:** Alvarez, Daniel
**Session Date:** 11/07/2025
**Locations Observed:** 96 Geiger ICF, Liverpool TEC, Chadwicks TEC
**Observing Staff:** Joseph Harris, CCC-SLP

---

## ENVIRONMENTAL TRIGGER DOCUMENTATION

**TRANSITION 1:** 96 Geiger ICF → Liverpool TEC
Time: 10:15 AM
Trigger: Unexpected staff change (regular driver unavailable)
Client Response: Moderate anxiety, verbal questioning, increased pacing

Daniel demonstrated heightened anxiety when informed of transition from 
96 Geiger ICF to Liverpool TEC with unfamiliar driver. 
Environmental factors noted:
- Different vehicle than typical transport
- Substitute staff member instead of usual Joseph Harris, CCC-SLP

**TRANSITION 2:** Liverpool TEC → Chadwicks TEC
Time: 11:45 AM
Trigger: Schedule modification due to building maintenance
Client Response: Mild agitation, requesting return to familiar setting

**SCHEDULE DISRUPTION ANALYSIS:**
Originally scheduled appointment with Dr. Barnes at Liverpool TEC on 
04/14/2026 was 
rescheduled to 05/03/2026 
due to provider illness. Daniel exhibited increased anxiety and repetitive questioning 
about appointment status.

**PARENT CONTACT:**
Justin Alvarez contacted at (315) 434-7890 to discuss 
schedule sensitivity. Parent reported Daniel frequently references upcoming appointments 
at home and struggles with last-minute changes.

**SENSORY ENVIRONMENT ASSESSMENT:**
96 Geiger ICF: Familiar lighting, low noise level, preferred seating available
Liverpool TEC: Moderate noise level, fluorescent lighting, multiple peer interactions
Chadwicks TEC: High activity level, variable noise, open floor plan

Consultation with Dr. Hill scheduled for 5/23/2026 
to assess sensory processing needs and environmental accommodation recommendations.

**RECOMMENDATIONS:**
- Increase transition warnings from 5 minutes to 15 minutes advance notice
- Environmental modifications at Liverpool TEC:
  * Provide noise-canceling headphones during high-activity periods
  * Designate quiet space for breaks
- Schedule consistency protocol - avoid changes within 48 hours when possible
- Provider coordination for appointment preparation with visual schedule

**FOLLOW-UP:**
Meeting with Justin Alvarez scheduled 
05/08/2026 
to review environmental sensitivities.

Contact Dr. Hill at 315-435-8901 for sensory consultation.

**Documented by:** Joseph Harris, CCC-SLP
**Date:** 11/07/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

**Program:** Chadwicks TEC
**Time:** 9:00 AM - 10:00 AM
**Behavior Specialist:** Grace Nguyen

---

## SKILL ACQUISITION SESSION

**Target Skill:** Multi-step vocational task completion
**Teaching Method:** Discrete trial training with naturalistic teaching

**SESSION SUMMARY:**
Matthew participated in 45 discrete trial training sessions focusing on lunch service 
preparation skills at Chadwicks TEC. Session began at 9:00 AM with 
hand washing and apron donning.

**TRIAL DATA:**
- Trial block 1: 80% accuracy across 15 trials
- Trial block 2: 90% accuracy across 15 trials  
- Trial block 3: 95% accuracy across 15 trials
- Overall session accuracy: 85%

**PROMPTING HIERARCHY:**
Initial trials required full physical prompting, progressing to verbal prompting only by session end. 
Matthew demonstrated improvement in response latency from 8.5 seconds to 3.2 seconds.

**VOCATIONAL INTEGRATION:**
Matthew practiced food service skills during lunch preparation. Staff Owen Kelly, Psy.D. supervised and reported successful completion of assigned tasks with minimal support.

**PARENT COLLABORATION:**
Contacted Shirley Scott at (315)452-4567 to discuss home practice strategies. 
Parent reported Matthew has been practicing sorting tasks at home with good success.

**NEXT SESSION GOALS:**
- Increase trial complexity for vocational skills
- Reduce prompting to gestural level only
- Incorporate generalization setting

**Therapist:** Grace Nguyen
**Date signed:** 10/25/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

# UCP SESSION NOTE - MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR

**Client:** Cruz, Daniel
**Incident Date:** 10/28/2025
**Incident Time:** 10:45 AM
**Location:** 92 Geiger ICF
**Staff Present:** Jackson Evans

---

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
Daniel was engaged in art activity at 92 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Daniel exhibited Minor non-compliance characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 2 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff Jackson Evans implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

Daniel responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
4 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
Daniel participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Daniel was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with Sharon Cruz at 315.513.2345. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by Jackson Evans
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

**Next session:** 4/22/26 at 92 Geiger ICF
**Provider check-in:** Dr. Martinez on April 28, 2026

**Report filed by:** Jackson Evans
**Filed:** 10/28/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

---

## POSITIVE SOCIAL ENGAGEMENT SESSION

Daniel demonstrated exceptional social skills during structured group activity at 
Chadwicks TEC from 10:00 AM to 12:00 PM.

**PEER INTERACTIONS:**
Daniel engaged appropriately with peers Noah and Sophia during board game activity. 
Initiated 9 social interactions, including:
- Sharing game pieces with Noah
- Inviting Sophia to join activity
- Requesting turn-taking using functional communication strategies

**COMMUNICATION SUCCESSES:**
Following recommendations from Dr. Bryant, Daniel utilized total communication approach 
effectively. Verbally expressed wants/needs 11 times throughout session.

**STAFF INTERACTIONS:**
Responded positively to prompts from Aria Hernandez and Ethan Martinez. 
Built rapport through shared interest in activities. Accepted redirection appropriately when needed.

**GROUP ACTIVITY PARTICIPATION:**
Activity: Cooperative board game
Duration: 45 minutes
Peers present: Noah, Sophia
Adult supervision: 1:3 staff-to-client ratio

**PARENT FEEDBACK:**
Robert Morris attended pickup and reported Daniel has 
been initiating play with siblings at home more frequently. Contact maintained via daily communication log.

**RECOMMENDATIONS:**
- Continue social skills group at Chadwicks TEC
- Increase peer interaction opportunities during unstructured time
- Collaborate with Dr. Bryant for social-emotional assessment

**Documentation:** Aria Hernandez
**Date:** 10/27/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

# UCP SESSION NOTE - MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR

**Client:** Henry Sanders
**Incident Date:** 10/21/2025
**Incident Time:** 10:45 AM
**Location:** 88 Geiger ICF
**Staff Present:** Logan Kim

---

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
Henry was engaged in art activity at 88 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Henry exhibited Verbal refusal characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 3 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff Logan Kim implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

Henry responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
5 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
Henry participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Henry was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with Michelle Sanders at 315.513.2345. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by Logan Kim
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

**Next session:** April 22, 2026 at 88 Geiger ICF
**Provider check-in:** Dr. Ross on 4/28/2026

**Report filed by:** Logan Kim
**Filed:** 10/21/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

Duration: Escalation 5 minutes, restraint 22 minutes

1. Therapeutic processing of incident
2. Safety planning reinforcement
3. Skill rebuilding for emotion regulation
4. Relationship repair with staff and peers

- Event sequence understanding using visual timeline
- Emotional identification (anger, frustration, feeling out of control)

- Safety understanding (why restraint was necessary)

recognized inappropriate choice and impact on others.

Reviewed and updated safety protocols with Abigail.

- Increased evening anxiety medication
- Continue current regimen with modifications

Focus areas identified:

- Break request training as needed throughout day

**Client:** Sofia M. Gutierrez
**Incident Date:** 10/12/2025
**Incident Time:** 10:45 AM
**Location:** 100 Geiger ICF

---

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
Sofia was engaged in art activity at 100 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Sofia exhibited Verbal refusal characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 4 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff Owen Lewis implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

Sofia responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
6 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
Sofia participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Sofia was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with Anthony Gutierrez at (315) 477-5678. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by Owen Lewis
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

**Next session:** 4/22/2026 at 100 Geiger ICF
**Provider check-in:** Logan Wilson, MS, CCC-SLP on 5/04/2026

**Report filed by:** Owen Lewis
**Filed:** 10/12/2025

**Target Skill:** Multi-step vocational task completion
**Teaching Method:** Discrete trial training with naturalistic teaching

**SESSION SUMMARY:**
Zoey participated in 45 discrete trial training sessions focusing on lunch service 
preparation skills at Chadwicks TEC. Session began at 2:00 PM with 
hand washing and apron donning.

- Trial block 2: 87% accuracy across 15 trials  
- Trial block 3: 88% accuracy across 15 trials
- Overall session accuracy: 81%

Initial trials required full physical prompting, progressing to verbal prompting only by session end. 
Zoey demonstrated improvement in response latency from 8.5 seconds to 3.2 seconds.

**VOCATIONAL INTEGRATION:**
Zoey practiced food service skills during lunch preparation. Staff Liam Ramos, BCBA supervised and reported successful completion of assigned tasks with minimal support.

**PARENT COLLABORATION:**
Contacted Steven Jackson at (315) 508-1234 to discuss home practice strategies. 
Parent reported Zoey has been practicing sorting tasks at home with good success.

- Increase trial complexity for vocational skills
- Reduce prompting to gestural level only
- Incorporate generalization setting

**Teaching Method:** Discrete trial training with naturalistic teaching

preparation skills at Chadwicks TEC. Session began at 10:00 AM with 
hand washing and apron donning.

Contacted Sandra Kim at 315.440.7890 to discuss home practice strategies. 
Parent reported John has been practicing sorting tasks at home with good success.

**NEXT SESSION GOALS:**
- Increase trial complexity for vocational skills
- Reduce prompting to gestural level only
- Incorporate generalization setting

**Therapist:** Isabella Johnson, BCBA, LBA
**Date signed:** 11/28/2025

**Client:** Ramirez, Isabella
**Incident Date:** 10/15/2025
**Incident Time:** 10:45 AM
**Location:** 88 Geiger ICF
**Staff Present:** William Brown

---

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
Isabella was engaged in art activity at 88 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Isabella exhibited Verbal refusal characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 3 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff William Brown implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

Isabella responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
4 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
Isabella participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Isabella was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with Richard Ramirez at 315.429.8901. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by William Brown
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

**Next session:** 4/22/26 at 88 Geiger ICF

**Client:** Emma Ortiz D.

**Incident Time:** 2:15 PM
**Location:** 100 Geiger ICF

---

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
Emma was engaged in art activity at 100 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Emma exhibited Verbal refusal characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 3 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff Lucas Campbell implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

Emma responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
7 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
Emma participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Emma was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with Sarah Ortiz at 315.445.7890. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by Lucas Campbell
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

**Next session:** 4/22/26 at 100 Geiger ICF

# UCP SESSION NOTE - SKILL ACQUISITION

**Client:** Sanders, Luke P.
**Date of Birth:** 06/26/2011
**Session Date:** 10/15/2025
**Program:** Liverpool TEC
**Time:** 2:00 PM - 3:30 PM
**Behavior Specialist:** Charlotte Lee

---

## SKILL ACQUISITION SESSION

**Target Skill:** Multi-step vocational task completion
**Teaching Method:** Discrete trial training with naturalistic teaching

**SESSION SUMMARY:**
Luke participated in 45 discrete trial training sessions focusing on lunch service 
preparation skills at Liverpool TEC. Session began at 2:00 PM with 
hand washing and apron donning.

**TRIAL DATA:**
- Trial block 1: 70% accuracy across 15 trials
- Trial block 2: 81% accuracy across 15 trials  
- Trial block 3: 87% accuracy across 15 trials
- Overall session accuracy: 80%

**PROMPTING HIERARCHY:**

# UCP POST-CRISIS RECOVERY SESSION NOTE

**Client:** Emily Lopez D.
**Recovery Session Date:** 11/27/2025
**Original Incident Date:** 04/18/2026
**Location:** 96 Geiger ICF
**Staff:** Ava Morris
**Clinical Supervisor:** Amelia Nguyen, LMFT

---

## POST-CRISIS THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTION

**INCIDENT REFERENCE:**
Critical incident on 04/18/2026 at 96 Geiger ICF.
Incident Report ID: INC-2026-7757
Type: Physical aggression toward peer and staff, property destruction
Duration: Escalation 5 minutes, restraint 18 minutes

TIME SINCE INCIDENT: 48 hours

**CURRENT SESSION PURPOSE:**
1. Therapeutic processing of incident
2. Safety planning reinforcement
3. Skill rebuilding for emotion regulation
4. Relationship repair with staff and peers

**SESSION ACTIVITIES:**

**THERAPEUTIC PROCESSING:**
Emily participated in cognitive-behavioral processing with Ava Morris.

Discussion topics:
- Event sequence understanding using visual timeline
- Emotional identification (anger, frustration, feeling out of control)
- Alternative response strategies (asking for break, using calm-down space)
- Safety understanding (why restraint was necessary)

Emily's insight: Demonstrated good understanding of event sequence, identified trigger, 
recognized inappropriate choice and impact on others.

**SAFETY PLANNING:**
Reviewed and updated safety protocols with Emily.

**NEW SAFETY MEASURES IMPLEMENTED:**
Following incident on 04/18/2026:
1. Individual activity schedule - Implemented 4/19/2026
2. Enhanced visual supports for emotion regulation - Implemented April 19, 2026
3. Enhanced monitoring during peer activities (1:2 ratio)

**PARENT COLLABORATION:**
Joint session with Barbara Lopez.

Parents contacted at 315-435-8901 to confirm session attendance.

Discussion points:
- Home-program consistency for emotion regulation strategies
- Warning sign recognition (escalating voice volume, body tension, pacing)
- De-escalation support at home (offering break space, reducing demands)
- Communication protocols between home and program

**STAFF RELATIONSHIP REPAIR:**
Emily met individually with staff involved in incident.
Facilitated by: Amelia Nguyen, LMFT

Process included: Emily's verbal apology, staff reassurance of continued support, 
discussion of moving forward. Staff reported positive interaction quality.

**BEHAVIORAL SUPPORT PLAN UPDATES:**
Modified BSP implemented 4/19/2026 following comprehensive review.

Changes include:
- Enhanced antecedent strategies (increased warnings before transitions)
- Additional teaching of replacement behaviors (requesting break using visual card)
- Updated crisis protocols (specific de-escalation sequence)
- Modified reinforcement schedule

Review team:
- Levi Williams, MS, CCC-SLP (Behavior Specialist)
- Dr. Mitchell (Occupational Therapist)
- Dr. Aung (Speech-Language Pathologist)
- Lucas Campbell, M.S. (Nursing)
- Parents: Barbara Lopez

**PSYCHIATRIC FOLLOW-UP:**
Emergency consultation with Scarlett Ramirez, NP on April 19, 2026.

Medication adjustments:
- Increased evening anxiety medication
- Continue current regimen with modifications

Next psychiatric appointment: 5/24/26

**SKILL REBUILDING:**
Focus areas identified:
1. Emotion regulation and identification
2. Requesting breaks appropriately
3. Appropriate peer interactions

Teaching sessions scheduled:
- Daily emotion identification practice with Ava Morris
- Twice weekly skills practice
- Break request training as needed throughout day

**ENVIRONMENTAL MODIFICATIONS:**
Changes made at 96 Geiger ICF following incident:

Physical environment:
- Designated "calm corner" with visual supports (Completed 4/19/2026)
- Additional soft seating for de-escalation space

Schedule modifications:
- Individual time for preferred activities
- Structured peer activities with higher staff ratio for 1 week

**MONITORING PROTOCOL:**
Enhanced monitoring period: 11/27/2025 through 5/4/2026 (2 weeks)

Monitoring frequency: Hourly emotion check-ins using 5-point scale
Documentation: Electronic incident tracking system + daily narrative notes

**CHECK-IN SCHEDULE:**
Daily check-ins with rotating staff:
- Morning: 8:30 AM (baseline mood assessment)
- Midday: 12:00 PM (activity participation check)
- Afternoon: 3:00 PM (end-of-day processing)

**PARENT COMMUNICATION PLAN:**
Daily updates to Barbara Lopez:
- Method: Phone call
- Time: 4:00 PM daily
- Contact: 315-435-8901

**PROGRESS INDICATORS:**
Since incident on 04/18/2026 (48 hours post-incident):
- Zero physical aggression incidents
- Appropriate use of break request card 4 times
- Positive peer interactions during structured activities (100% appropriate)
- Verbal communication of emotions using 5-point scale with 83% accuracy

**NEXT STEPS:**
☑ Continue daily monitoring through 5/4/2026
☑ BSP implementation fidelity checks (daily by supervisor)
☑ Ongoing parent collaboration (daily calls)
☑ Psychiatric follow-up 5/23/2026
☑ Incident review team meeting scheduled
☑ FBA update completion target: May 1, 2026

**DOCUMENTATION:**
Recovery session documented by: Ava Morris
Clinical supervision: Amelia Nguyen, LMFT
Parent consent obtained: 11/27/2025
Treatment plan updated: 4/19/26

Session date: 11/27/2025
Next recovery session: April 27, 2026

**Client:** Aiden Scott
**Incident Date:** 11/08/2025
**Incident Time:** 11:20 AM
**Location:** 100 Geiger ICF
**Staff Present:** Wyatt Johnson

---

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
Aiden was engaged in art activity at 100 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Aiden exhibited Brief withdrawal characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 3 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff Wyatt Johnson implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

Aiden responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
7 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
Aiden participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Aiden was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with Emily Scott at (315)457-4567. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by Wyatt Johnson
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

**Next session:** April 22, 2026 at 100 Geiger ICF
**Provider check-in:** Dr. Cooper on 05/03/2026

**Report filed by:** Wyatt Johnson
**Filed:** 11/08/2025

# UCP SESSION NOTE - MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR

**Client:** Ross, Zoey
**Incident Date:** 10/21/2025
**Incident Time:** 11:20 AM
**Location:** 92 Geiger ICF
**Staff Present:** Elijah Lewis, M.Ed.

---

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
Zoey was engaged in art activity at 92 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Zoey exhibited Verbal refusal characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 5 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff Elijah Lewis, M.Ed. implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

Zoey responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
7 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
Zoey participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Zoey was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with Samuel Ross at 315-443-9012. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by Elijah Lewis
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

**Next session:** 4/22/2026 at 92 Geiger ICF
**Provider check-in:** Dr. Foster on 04/29/2026

**Report filed by:** Elijah Lewis, M.Ed.
**Filed:** 10/21/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

**Client:** Jimenez, Chloe M.

**Original Incident Date:** 04/18/2026
**Location:** 92 Geiger ICF
**Staff:** Evelyn Garcia
**Clinical Supervisor:** Liam Allen, BCBA

---

## POST-CRISIS THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTION

**INCIDENT REFERENCE:**
Critical incident on 04/18/2026 at 92 Geiger ICF.
Incident Report ID: INC-2026-6212
Type: Physical aggression toward peer and staff, property destruction
Duration: Escalation 7 minutes, restraint 22 minutes

TIME SINCE INCIDENT: 48 hours

**CURRENT SESSION PURPOSE:**
1. Therapeutic processing of incident
2. Safety planning reinforcement
3. Skill rebuilding for emotion regulation
4. Relationship repair with staff and peers

**SESSION ACTIVITIES:**

**THERAPEUTIC PROCESSING:**
Chloe participated in cognitive-behavioral processing with Evelyn Garcia.

Discussion topics:
- Event sequence understanding using visual timeline
- Emotional identification (anger, frustration, feeling out of control)
- Alternative response strategies (asking for break, using calm-down space)
- Safety understanding (why restraint was necessary)

Chloe's insight: Demonstrated good understanding of event sequence, identified trigger, 
recognized inappropriate choice and impact on others.

**SAFETY PLANNING:**
Reviewed and updated safety protocols with Chloe.

**NEW SAFETY MEASURES IMPLEMENTED:**
Following incident on 04/18/2026:
1. Individual activity schedule - Implemented 4/19/26
2. Enhanced visual supports for emotion regulation - Implemented 4/19/2026
3. Enhanced monitoring during peer activities (1:2 ratio)

**PARENT COLLABORATION:**
Joint session with Patricia Jimenez and Gregory Jimenez.

Parents contacted at 315.490.2345 to confirm session attendance.

Discussion points:
- Home-program consistency for emotion regulation strategies
- Warning sign recognition (escalating voice volume, body tension, pacing)
- De-escalation support at home (offering break space, reducing demands)
- Communication protocols between home and program

**STAFF RELATIONSHIP REPAIR:**
Chloe met individually with staff involved in incident.
Facilitated by: Liam Allen, BCBA

Process included: Chloe's verbal apology, staff reassurance of continued support, 
discussion of moving forward. Staff reported positive interaction quality.

**BEHAVIORAL SUPPORT PLAN UPDATES:**
Modified BSP implemented April 19, 2026 following comprehensive review.

Changes include:
- Enhanced antecedent strategies (increased warnings before transitions)
- Additional teaching of replacement behaviors (requesting break using visual card)
- Updated crisis protocols (specific de-escalation sequence)
- Modified reinforcement schedule

Review team:
- Aubrey Gray, MS, CCC-SLP (Behavior Specialist)
- Dr. Perry (Occupational Therapist)
- Daniel Evans, CNS (Speech-Language Pathologist)
- Dr. Henderson (Nursing)
- Parents: Patricia Jimenez, Gregory Jimenez

**PSYCHIATRIC FOLLOW-UP:**
Emergency consultation with Dr. Cook on April 19, 2026.

Medication adjustments:
- Dosage adjustment made
- Continue current regimen with modifications

Next psychiatric appointment: 5/25/2026

**SKILL REBUILDING:**
Focus areas identified:
1. Emotion regulation and identification
2. Requesting breaks appropriately
3. Appropriate peer interactions

Teaching sessions scheduled:
- Daily emotion identification practice with Evelyn Garcia
- Twice weekly skills practice
- Break request training as needed throughout day

**ENVIRONMENTAL MODIFICATIONS:**
Changes made at 92 Geiger ICF following incident:

Physical environment:
- Designated "calm corner" with visual supports (Completed April 19, 2026)
- Additional soft seating for de-escalation space

Schedule modifications:
- Individual time for preferred activities
- Structured peer activities with higher staff ratio for 1 week

**MONITORING PROTOCOL:**
Enhanced monitoring period: 10/08/2025 through 5/4/26 (2 weeks)

Monitoring frequency: Hourly emotion check-ins using 5-point scale
Documentation: Electronic incident tracking system + daily narrative notes

**CHECK-IN SCHEDULE:**
Daily check-ins with rotating staff:
- Morning: 8:30 AM (baseline mood assessment)
- Midday: 12:00 PM (activity participation check)
- Afternoon: 3:00 PM (end-of-day processing)

**PARENT COMMUNICATION PLAN:**
Daily updates to Patricia Jimenez:
- Method: Phone call
- Time: 4:00 PM daily
- Contact: 315.490.2345

**PROGRESS INDICATORS:**
Since incident on 04/18/2026 (48 hours post-incident):
- Zero physical aggression incidents
- Appropriate use of break request card 3 times
- Positive peer interactions during structured activities (100% appropriate)
- Verbal communication of emotions using 5-point scale with 88% accuracy

**NEXT STEPS:**
☑ Continue daily monitoring through 5/4/26
☑ BSP implementation fidelity checks (daily by supervisor)
☑ Ongoing parent collaboration (daily calls)
☑ Psychiatric follow-up May 18, 2026
☑ Incident review team meeting scheduled
☑ FBA update completion target: May 1, 2026

**DOCUMENTATION:**
Recovery session documented by: Evelyn Garcia
Clinical supervision: Liam Allen, BCBA

Treatment plan updated: 4/19/26

Next recovery session: 4/27/26

- Reduce prompting to gestural level only
- Incorporate generalization setting

preparation skills at Baldwinsville TEC. Session began at 2:00 PM with

Parent reported Matthew has been practicing sorting tasks at home with good success.

**NEXT SESSION GOALS:**
- Increase trial complexity for vocational skills
- Reduce prompting to gestural level only
- Incorporate generalization setting

**Therapist:** Jacob Howard
**Date signed:** 10/23/2025

**INCIDENT REFERENCE:**
Critical incident on 4/18/2026 at 88 Geiger ICF.
Incident Report ID: INC-2026-2509
Type: Physical aggression toward peer and staff, property destruction
Duration: Escalation 6 minutes, restraint 24 minutes

TIME SINCE INCIDENT: 48 hours

**CURRENT SESSION PURPOSE:**
1. Therapeutic processing of incident
2. Safety planning reinforcement
3. Skill rebuilding for emotion regulation
4. Relationship repair with staff and peers

**SESSION ACTIVITIES:**

**THERAPEUTIC PROCESSING:**
Aria participated in cognitive-behavioral processing with Riley Richardson.

Discussion topics:
- Event sequence understanding using visual timeline
- Emotional identification (anger, frustration, feeling out of control)
- Alternative response strategies (asking for break, using calm-down space)
- Safety understanding (why restraint was necessary)

Aria's insight: Demonstrated good understanding of event sequence, identified trigger, 
recognized inappropriate choice and impact on others.

**SAFETY PLANNING:**
Reviewed and updated safety protocols with Aria.

**NEW SAFETY MEASURES IMPLEMENTED:**
Following incident on 4/18/2026:
1. Individual activity schedule - Implemented 4/19/2026
2. Enhanced visual supports for emotion regulation - Implemented 4/19/26
3. Enhanced monitoring during peer activities (1:2 ratio)

**PARENT COLLABORATION:**
Joint session with Jennifer Ruiz and Jacob Ruiz.

Parents contacted at (315) 445-7890 to confirm session attendance.

Discussion points:
- Home-program consistency for emotion regulation strategies
- Warning sign recognition (escalating voice volume, body tension, pacing)
- De-escalation support at home (offering break space, reducing demands)
- Communication protocols between home and program

**STAFF RELATIONSHIP REPAIR:**
Aria met individually with staff involved in incident.
Facilitated by: Emma Cox, BSN

Process included: Aria's verbal apology, staff reassurance of continued support, 
discussion of moving forward. Staff reported positive interaction quality.

**BEHAVIORAL SUPPORT PLAN UPDATES:**
Modified BSP implemented April 19, 2026 following comprehensive review.

Changes include:
- Enhanced antecedent strategies (increased warnings before transitions)
- Additional teaching of replacement behaviors (requesting break using visual card)
- Updated crisis protocols (specific de-escalation sequence)
- Modified reinforcement schedule

Review team:
- Logan Ward, Ed.M. (Behavior Specialist)
- Dr. Harris (Occupational Therapist)
- Amelia Gonzales, RN (Speech-Language Pathologist)
- Dr. Clark (Nursing)
- Parents: Jennifer Ruiz, Jacob Ruiz

Emergency consultation with Dr. Allen on 4/19/2026.

Medication adjustments:
- Dosage adjustment made
- Continue current regimen with modifications

Next psychiatric appointment: 05/21/2026

**SKILL REBUILDING:**
Focus areas identified:
1. Emotion regulation and identification
2. Requesting breaks appropriately
3. Appropriate peer interactions

Teaching sessions scheduled:
- Daily emotion identification practice with Riley Richardson
- Twice weekly skills practice
- Break request training as needed throughout day

**ENVIRONMENTAL MODIFICATIONS:**
Changes made at 88 Geiger ICF following incident:

Physical environment:
- Designated "calm corner" with visual supports (Completed 4/19/26)
- Additional soft seating for de-escalation space

- Individual time for preferred activities
- Structured peer activities with higher staff ratio for 1 week

# UCP SESSION NOTE - MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR

**Client:** Gomez, Jackson
**Incident Date:** 11/27/2025
**Incident Time:** 11:20 AM
**Location:** 88 Geiger ICF
**Staff Present:** Henry Myers

---

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
Jackson was engaged in art activity at 88 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Jackson exhibited Minor non-compliance characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 4 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff Henry Myers implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

Jackson responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
5 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
Jackson participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Jackson was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with Diane Gomez at 315-434-7890. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by Henry Myers
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

**Next session:** 4/22/2026 at 88 Geiger ICF
**Provider check-in:** Dr. Butler on 05/05/2026

**Report filed by:** Henry Myers
**Filed:** 11/27/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

# UCP SESSION NOTE - MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR

**Client:** Luke Roberts
**Incident Date:** 11/13/2025
**Incident Time:** 2:15 PM
**Location:** 88 Geiger ICF
**Staff Present:** David Mendoza

---

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
Luke was engaged in art activity at 88 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Luke exhibited Brief withdrawal characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 4 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff David Mendoza implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

Luke responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
4 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
Luke participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Luke was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with Susan Roberts at (315)438-7890. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by David Mendoza
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

**Next session:** 4/22/26 at 88 Geiger ICF
**Provider check-in:** Dr. Mitchell on 5/05/2026

**Report filed by:** David Mendoza
**Filed:** 11/13/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

# UCP POST-CRISIS RECOVERY SESSION NOTE

**Client:** Jackson Jones
**Recovery Session Date:** 10/09/2025
**Original Incident Date:** 4/18/26
**Location:** 100 Geiger ICF
**Staff:** Henry Watson
**Clinical Supervisor:** Amelia Phillips, Behavior Specialist, M.Ed.

---

## POST-CRISIS THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTION

**INCIDENT REFERENCE:**
Critical incident on 4/18/26 at 100 Geiger ICF.
Incident Report ID: INC-2026-8298
Type: Physical aggression toward peer and staff, property destruction
Duration: Escalation 8 minutes, restraint 25 minutes

TIME SINCE INCIDENT: 48 hours

**CURRENT SESSION PURPOSE:**
1. Therapeutic processing of incident
2. Safety planning reinforcement
3. Skill rebuilding for emotion regulation
4. Relationship repair with staff and peers

**SESSION ACTIVITIES:**

**THERAPEUTIC PROCESSING:**
Jackson participated in cognitive-behavioral processing with Henry Watson.

Discussion topics:
- Event sequence understanding using visual timeline
- Emotional identification (anger, frustration, feeling out of control)
- Alternative response strategies (asking for break, using calm-down space)
- Safety understanding (why restraint was necessary)

Jackson's insight: Demonstrated good understanding of event sequence, identified trigger, 
recognized inappropriate choice and impact on others.

**SAFETY PLANNING:**
Reviewed and updated safety protocols with Jackson.

**NEW SAFETY MEASURES IMPLEMENTED:**
Following incident on 4/18/26:
1. Individual activity schedule - Implemented 4/19/26
2. Enhanced visual supports for emotion regulation - Implemented April 19, 2026
3. Enhanced monitoring during peer activities (1:2 ratio)

**PARENT COLLABORATION:**
Joint session with Paul Jones.

Parents contacted at 315-464-5678 to confirm session attendance.

Discussion points:
- Home-program consistency for emotion regulation strategies
- Warning sign recognition (escalating voice volume, body tension, pacing)
- De-escalation support at home (offering break space, reducing demands)
- Communication protocols between home and program

**STAFF RELATIONSHIP REPAIR:**
Jackson met individually with staff involved in incident.
Facilitated by: Amelia Phillips, Behavior Specialist, M.Ed.

Process included: Jackson's verbal apology, staff reassurance of continued support, 
discussion of moving forward. Staff reported positive interaction quality.

**BEHAVIORAL SUPPORT PLAN UPDATES:**
Modified BSP implemented 4/19/26 following comprehensive review.

Changes include:
- Enhanced antecedent strategies (increased warnings before transitions)
- Additional teaching of replacement behaviors (requesting break using visual card)
- Updated crisis protocols (specific de-escalation sequence)
- Modified reinforcement schedule

Review team:
- Lily Foster, LCSW (Behavior Specialist)
- Dr. Raju (Occupational Therapist)
- Dr. Bailey (Speech-Language Pathologist)
- Dr. Hernandez (Nursing)
- Parents: Paul Jones

**PSYCHIATRIC FOLLOW-UP:**
Emergency consultation with James James, LCSW on 4/19/2026.

Medication adjustments:
- Dosage adjustment made
- Continue current regimen with modifications

Next psychiatric appointment: 05/18/2026

**SKILL REBUILDING:**
Focus areas identified:
1. Emotion regulation and identification
2. Requesting breaks appropriately
3. Appropriate peer interactions

Teaching sessions scheduled:
- Daily emotion identification practice with Henry Watson
- Twice weekly skills practice
- Break request training as needed throughout day

**ENVIRONMENTAL MODIFICATIONS:**
Changes made at 100 Geiger ICF following incident:

Physical environment:
- Designated "calm corner" with visual supports (Completed April 19, 2026)
- Additional soft seating for de-escalation space

Schedule modifications:
- Individual time for preferred activities
- Structured peer activities with higher staff ratio for 1 week

**MONITORING PROTOCOL:**
Enhanced monitoring period: 10/09/2025 through 5/4/2026 (2 weeks)

Monitoring frequency: Hourly emotion check-ins using 5-point scale
Documentation: Electronic incident tracking system + daily narrative notes

**CHECK-IN SCHEDULE:**
Daily check-ins with rotating staff:
- Morning: 8:30 AM (baseline mood assessment)
- Midday: 12:00 PM (activity participation check)
- Afternoon: 3:00 PM (end-of-day processing)

**PARENT COMMUNICATION PLAN:**
Daily updates to Paul Jones:
- Method: Phone call
- Time: 4:00 PM daily
- Contact: 315-464-5678

**PROGRESS INDICATORS:**
Since incident on 4/18/26 (48 hours post-incident):
- Zero physical aggression incidents
- Appropriate use of break request card 3 times
- Positive peer interactions during structured activities (100% appropriate)
- Verbal communication of emotions using 5-point scale with 76% accuracy

**NEXT STEPS:**
☑ Continue daily monitoring through 5/4/2026
☑ BSP implementation fidelity checks (daily by supervisor)
☑ Ongoing parent collaboration (daily calls)
☑ Psychiatric follow-up 5/10/2026
☑ Incident review team meeting scheduled
☑ FBA update completion target: 5/3/26

**DOCUMENTATION:**
Recovery session documented by: Henry Watson
Clinical supervision: Amelia Phillips, Behavior Specialist, M.Ed.
Parent consent obtained: 10/09/2025
Treatment plan updated: 4/19/26

Session date: 10/09/2025
Next recovery session: 4/27/2026

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

**Client:** C. Jones
**Incident Date:** 10/20/2025
**Incident Time:** 2:15 PM
**Location:** 96 Geiger ICF
**Staff Present:** Avery Hughes

---

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
Chloe was engaged in art activity at 96 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Chloe exhibited Minor non-compliance characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 4 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff Avery Hughes implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

Chloe responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
7 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
Chloe participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Chloe was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with Robert Jones at (315) 449-4567. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by Avery Hughes
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

**Next session:** April 22, 2026 at 96 Geiger ICF
**Provider check-in:** Emma Taylor, LMFT on May 4, 2026

**Report filed by:** Avery Hughes
**Filed:** 10/20/2025

# UCP SESSION NOTE - MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR

**Client:** Abigail Gomez
**Incident Date:** 11/12/2025
**Incident Time:** 10:45 AM
**Location:** 100 Geiger ICF
**Staff Present:** Chloe Cook

---

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
Abigail was engaged in art activity at 100 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Abigail exhibited Minor non-compliance characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 5 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff Chloe Cook implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

Abigail responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
5 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
Abigail participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Abigail was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with Patricia Gomez at (315)441-9012. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by Chloe Cook
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

**Next session:** 04/22/2026 at 100 Geiger ICF
**Provider check-in:** Dr. Bryant on April 29, 2026

**Report filed by:** Chloe Cook
**Filed:** 11/12/2025

---

# UCP SESSION NOTE - ENVIRONMENTAL TRIGGER ANALYSIS

**Client:** Bailey, Evelyn
**Session Date:** 11/20/2025
**Locations Observed:** 88 Geiger ICF, Syracuse TEC, Baldwinsville TEC
**Observing Staff:** Henry Martinez

---

## ENVIRONMENTAL TRIGGER DOCUMENTATION

**TRANSITION 1:** 88 Geiger ICF → Syracuse TEC
Time: 10:15 AM
Trigger: Unexpected staff change (regular driver unavailable)
Client Response: Moderate anxiety, verbal questioning, increased pacing

Evelyn demonstrated heightened anxiety when informed of transition from 
88 Geiger ICF to Syracuse TEC with unfamiliar driver. 
Environmental factors noted:
- Different vehicle than typical transport
- Substitute staff member instead of usual Henry Martinez

**TRANSITION 2:** Syracuse TEC → Baldwinsville TEC
Time: 2:15 PM
Trigger: Schedule modification due to building maintenance
Client Response: Mild agitation, requesting return to familiar setting

**SCHEDULE DISRUPTION ANALYSIS:**
Originally scheduled appointment with Olivia Reed, M.S. at Syracuse TEC on 
4/12/2026 was 
rescheduled to 5/5/2026 
due to provider illness. Evelyn exhibited increased anxiety and repetitive questioning 
about appointment status.

**PARENT CONTACT:**
Aaron Bailey contacted at 315.482.2345 to discuss 
schedule sensitivity. Parent reported Evelyn frequently references upcoming appointments 
at home and struggles with last-minute changes.

**SENSORY ENVIRONMENT ASSESSMENT:**
88 Geiger ICF: Familiar lighting, low noise level, preferred seating available
Syracuse TEC: Moderate noise level, fluorescent lighting, multiple peer interactions
Baldwinsville TEC: High activity level, variable noise, open floor plan

Consultation with Isabella Bailey, LMHC scheduled for May 20, 2026 
to assess sensory processing needs and environmental accommodation recommendations.

**RECOMMENDATIONS:**
- Increase transition warnings from 5 minutes to 15 minutes advance notice

**Incident Time:** 11:20 AM

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
Henry was engaged in art activity at 92 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Henry exhibited Minor non-compliance characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 2 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff David Sanders implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

Henry responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
4 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
Henry participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Henry was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with Eric Parker at (315) 457-4567. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by David Sanders
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

## POST-CRISIS THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTION

**INCIDENT REFERENCE:**
Critical incident on April 18, 2026 at 88 Geiger ICF.
Incident Report ID: INC-2026-9455
Type: Physical aggression toward peer and staff, property destruction
Duration: Escalation 7 minutes, restraint 24 minutes

TIME SINCE INCIDENT: 48 hours

**CURRENT SESSION PURPOSE:**
1. Therapeutic processing of incident
2. Safety planning reinforcement
3. Skill rebuilding for emotion regulation
4. Relationship repair with staff and peers

**SESSION ACTIVITIES:**

**THERAPEUTIC PROCESSING:**
Samuel participated in cognitive-behavioral processing with Julian Brooks, CCC-SLP.

Discussion topics:
- Event sequence understanding using visual timeline
- Emotional identification (anger, frustration, feeling out of control)
- Alternative response strategies (asking for break, using calm-down space)
- Safety understanding (why restraint was necessary)

Samuel's insight: Demonstrated good understanding of event sequence, identified trigger, 
recognized inappropriate choice and impact on others.

**SAFETY PLANNING:**
Reviewed and updated safety protocols with Samuel.

**NEW SAFETY MEASURES IMPLEMENTED:**
Following incident on April 18, 2026:
1. Individual activity schedule - Implemented 04/19/2026
2. Enhanced visual supports for emotion regulation - Implemented April 19, 2026
3. Enhanced monitoring during peer activities (1:2 ratio)

**PARENT COLLABORATION:**
Joint session with James Taylor.

Parents contacted at 315.492.5678 to confirm session attendance.

Discussion points:
- Home-program consistency for emotion regulation strategies
- Warning sign recognition (escalating voice volume, body tension, pacing)
- De-escalation support at home (offering break space, reducing demands)
- Communication protocols between home and program

**STAFF RELATIONSHIP REPAIR:**
Samuel met individually with staff involved in incident.
Facilitated by: Ava Kelly, BCBA

Process included: Samuel's verbal apology, staff reassurance of continued support, 
discussion of moving forward. Staff reported positive interaction quality.

**BEHAVIORAL SUPPORT PLAN UPDATES:**
Modified BSP implemented April 19, 2026 following comprehensive review.

Changes include:
- Enhanced antecedent strategies (increased warnings before transitions)
- Additional teaching of replacement behaviors (requesting break using visual card)
- Updated crisis protocols (specific de-escalation sequence)
- Modified reinforcement schedule

Review team:
- Matthew Edwards, Direct Support Professional (Behavior Specialist)
- Dr. Scanlon (Occupational Therapist)
- Dr. Gray (Speech-Language Pathologist)
- Daniel Gonzales, Psy.D. (Nursing)
- Parents: James Taylor

Emergency consultation with Dr. Hayes on 4/19/2026.

Medication adjustments:
- Added PRN protocol
- Continue current regimen with modifications

Next psychiatric appointment: 5/12/2026

**SKILL REBUILDING:**
Focus areas identified:
1. Emotion regulation and identification
2. Requesting breaks appropriately
3. Appropriate peer interactions

Teaching sessions scheduled:
- Daily emotion identification practice with Julian Brooks, CCC-SLP
- Twice weekly skills practice
- Break request training as needed throughout day

**ENVIRONMENTAL MODIFICATIONS:**
Changes made at 88 Geiger ICF following incident:

Physical environment:
- Designated "calm corner" with visual supports (Completed 4/19/2026)
- Additional soft seating for de-escalation space

Schedule modifications:
- Individual time for preferred activities
- Structured peer activities with higher staff ratio for 1 week

**MONITORING PROTOCOL:**
Enhanced monitoring period: 10/07/2025 through 5/4/26 (2 weeks)

Monitoring frequency: Hourly emotion check-ins using 5-point scale
Documentation: Electronic incident tracking system + daily narrative notes

**CHECK-IN SCHEDULE:**

- Morning: 8:30 AM (baseline mood assessment)

- Afternoon: 3:00 PM (end-of-day processing)

**PARENT COMMUNICATION PLAN:**
Daily updates to James Taylor:
- Method: Phone call
- Time: 4:00 PM daily
- Contact: 315.492.5678

Since incident on April 18, 2026 (48 hours post-incident):
- Zero physical aggression incidents
- Appropriate use of break request card 3 times
- Positive peer interactions during structured activities (100% appropriate)
- Verbal communication of emotions using 5-point scale with 78% accuracy

praise for appropriate choice-making.

Sebastian participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Sebastian was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**

intervention approach across settings.

# UCP SESSION NOTE - MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR

**Client:** M. Gutierrez
**Incident Date:** 11/08/2025
**Incident Time:** 10:45 AM
**Location:** 100 Geiger ICF
**Staff Present:** Jack Moore

---

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
Michael was engaged in art activity at 100 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Michael exhibited Verbal refusal characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 5 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff Jack Moore implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

Michael responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
4 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
Michael participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Michael was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with Anthony Gutierrez at (315)496-4567. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by Jack Moore
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

**Next session:** 4/22/2026 at 100 Geiger ICF
**Provider check-in:** Dr. Robinson on 5/4/26

**Report filed by:** Jack Moore
**Filed:** 11/08/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

---

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
Sofia was engaged in art activity at 95 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Sofia exhibited Brief withdrawal characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 4 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff Isabella Myers, CCC-SLP implemented:
1. Pause and proximity

Parent reported Sofia has been practicing sorting tasks at home with good success.

**NEXT SESSION GOALS:**
- Increase trial complexity for vocational skills
- Reduce prompting to gestural level only
- Incorporate generalization setting

**Therapist:** Harper Kim
**Date signed:** 10/22/2025

**INCIDENT REFERENCE:**
Critical incident on 04/18/2026 at 95 Geiger ICF.
Incident Report ID: INC-2026-8994
Type: Physical aggression toward peer and staff, property destruction
Duration: Escalation 6 minutes, restraint 22 minutes

TIME SINCE INCIDENT: 48 hours

**CURRENT SESSION PURPOSE:**
1. Therapeutic processing of incident
2. Safety planning reinforcement
3. Skill rebuilding for emotion regulation
4. Relationship repair with staff and peers

**SESSION ACTIVITIES:**

**THERAPEUTIC PROCESSING:**
Lily participated in cognitive-behavioral processing with Amelia Anderson.

Discussion topics:
- Event sequence understanding using visual timeline
- Emotional identification (anger, frustration, feeling out of control)
- Alternative response strategies (asking for break, using calm-down space)
- Safety understanding (why restraint was necessary)

Lily's insight: Demonstrated good understanding of event sequence, identified trigger, 
recognized inappropriate choice and impact on others.

**SAFETY PLANNING:**
Reviewed and updated safety protocols with Lily.

**NEW SAFETY MEASURES IMPLEMENTED:**
Following incident on 04/18/2026:
1. Individual activity schedule - Implemented April 19, 2026
2. Enhanced visual supports for emotion regulation - Implemented 04/19/2026
3. Enhanced monitoring during peer activities (1:2 ratio)

**PARENT COLLABORATION:**
Joint session with Carol James.

Parents contacted at 315-477-5678 to confirm session attendance.

Discussion points:
- Home-program consistency for emotion regulation strategies
- Warning sign recognition (escalating voice volume, body tension, pacing)
- De-escalation support at home (offering break space, reducing demands)
- Communication protocols between home and program

**STAFF RELATIONSHIP REPAIR:**
Lily met individually with staff involved in incident.
Facilitated by: Sophia Johnson, BCBA

Process included: Lily's verbal apology, staff reassurance of continued support, 
discussion of moving forward. Staff reported positive interaction quality.

Modified BSP implemented 04/19/2026 following comprehensive review.

Changes include:
- Enhanced antecedent strategies (increased warnings before transitions)
- Additional teaching of replacement behaviors (requesting break using visual card)
- Updated crisis protocols (specific de-escalation sequence)
- Modified reinforcement schedule

- Increased evening anxiety medication
- Continue current regimen with modifications

Focus areas identified:
1. Emotion regulation and identification
2. Requesting breaks appropriately
3. Appropriate peer interactions

Teaching sessions scheduled:
- Daily emotion identification practice with Amelia Anderson
- Twice weekly skills practice
- Break request training as needed throughout day

**ENVIRONMENTAL MODIFICATIONS:**

Physical environment:
- Designated "calm corner" with visual supports (Completed 4/19/2026)

- Individual time for preferred activities

**Teaching Method:** Discrete trial training with naturalistic teaching

Julian participated in 45 discrete trial training sessions focusing on lunch service 
preparation skills at Cicero TEC. Session began at 10:00 AM with 
hand washing and apron donning.

Parent reported Julian has been practicing sorting tasks at home with good success.

**NEXT SESSION GOALS:**
- Increase trial complexity for vocational skills
- Reduce prompting to gestural level only
- Incorporate generalization setting

# UCP SESSION NOTE - MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR

**Client:** Bennett, Charlotte
**Incident Date:** 11/23/2025
**Incident Time:** 2:15 PM
**Location:** 95 Geiger ICF
**Staff Present:** Aria Ross

---

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
Charlotte was engaged in art activity at 95 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Charlotte exhibited Brief withdrawal characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 4 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff Aria Ross implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

Charlotte responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
7 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
Charlotte participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Charlotte was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with Richard Bennett at (315) 436-7890. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by Aria Ross
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

**Next session:** 04/22/2026 at 95 Geiger ICF
**Provider check-in:** Matthew Butler, BSN on 5/01/2026

**Report filed by:** Aria Ross
**Filed:** 11/23/2025

# UCP SESSION NOTE - MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR

**Client:** R. Baker
**Incident Date:** 10/09/2025
**Incident Time:** 2:15 PM
**Location:** 95 Geiger ICF
**Staff Present:** Lily Carter

---

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
Riley was engaged in art activity at 95 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Riley exhibited Verbal refusal characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 4 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff Lily Carter implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

Riley responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
7 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
Riley participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Riley was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with Catherine Baker at 315-458-5678. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by Lily Carter
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

**Next session:** 4/22/26 at 95 Geiger ICF
**Provider check-in:** Dr. Morris on May 2, 2026

**Report filed by:** Lily Carter
**Filed:** 10/09/2025

- Reduce prompting to gestural level only
- Incorporate generalization setting

David Martin, Ph.D. joined intervention team.

Samuel responded to planned ignoring combined with blocking strategy.

Samuel returned to baseline. Moved to quiet room for recovery.

Carter Kelly, MS, CCC-SLP notified via phone message. Appointment maintained for

# UCP SESSION NOTE - SKILL ACQUISITION

**Client:** David J. Adams
**Date of Birth:** 12/16/2020
**Session Date:** 11/16/2025
**Program:** Cicero TEC
**Time:** 10:00 AM - 11:30 AM
**Behavior Specialist:** Aiden Young

---

## SKILL ACQUISITION SESSION

**Target Skill:** Multi-step vocational task completion
**Teaching Method:** Discrete trial training with naturalistic teaching

**SESSION SUMMARY:**
David participated in 45 discrete trial training sessions focusing on lunch service 
preparation skills at Cicero TEC. Session began at 10:00 AM with 
hand washing and apron donning.

**TRIAL DATA:**
- Trial block 1: 79% accuracy across 15 trials
- Trial block 2: 85% accuracy across 15 trials  
- Trial block 3: 89% accuracy across 15 trials
- Overall session accuracy: 79%

**PROMPTING HIERARCHY:**
Initial trials required full physical prompting, progressing to verbal prompting only by session end. 
David demonstrated improvement in response latency from 8.5 seconds to 3.2 seconds.

**VOCATIONAL INTEGRATION:**
David practiced food service skills during lunch preparation. Staff Noah Sanchez, Ed.M. supervised and reported successful completion of assigned tasks with minimal support.

**PARENT COLLABORATION:**
Contacted Linda Adams at (315) 431-8901 to discuss home practice strategies. 
Parent reported David has been practicing sorting tasks at home with good success.

**NEXT SESSION GOALS:**
- Increase trial complexity for vocational skills
- Reduce prompting to gestural level only
- Incorporate generalization setting

**Therapist:** Aiden Young
**Date signed:** 11/16/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

# UCP SESSION NOTE - MODERATE CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR

**UPSTATE CARING PARTNERS**
125 Business Park Drive, Utica, NY 13502
Phone: 315-724-6907

**Client Name:** Noah Thomas
**Date of Birth:** 8/21/20
**Incident Date:** 11/16/2025
**Incident Time:** 3:45 PM
**Location:** 96 Geiger ICF
**Staff Involved:** Emily Morgan; Aubrey Parker, LCSW

---

## MODERATE CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - MULTIPLE INTERVENTIONS

**INDIVIDUALS PRESENT:**
Staff: Emily Morgan; Aubrey Parker, LCSW
Location: Community room, 96 Geiger ICF

**INCIDENT TIMELINE:**

2:10 PM - ANTECEDENT
Noah was participating in group activity when transition announcement was made 
to end preferred activity.

2:15 PM - BEHAVIOR ONSET
Noah engaged in physical aggression including:
- Pushing peer
- Throwing materials
- Verbal aggression (yelling, protesting)

3:47 PM - INITIAL INTERVENTION
Emily Morgan implemented verbal de-escalation and visual supports.
Limited effectiveness. Behavior escalated to Level 2 (moderate severity).

2:20 PM - SECONDARY INTERVENTION
Aubrey Parker, LCSW joined intervention team.
SCIP-R blocking pads utilized per BSP protocol.
Noah responded to planned ignoring combined with blocking strategy.

2:28 PM - DE-ESCALATION ACHIEVED
Noah returned to baseline. Moved to quiet room for recovery.

**INJURIES/DAMAGE:**
Staff: Emily Morgan sustained minor scratch on left forearm, no medical treatment required
Property: Game materials damaged, approximate cost $28

# UCP SESSION NOTE - MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR

**Client:** Brooks, Wyatt
**Incident Date:** 10/10/2025
**Incident Time:** 10:45 AM
**Location:** 92 Geiger ICF
**Staff Present:** Sebastian Cruz

---

## MILD CHALLENGING BEHAVIOR - SUCCESSFULLY REDIRECTED

**ANTECEDENT:**
Wyatt was engaged in art activity at 92 Geiger ICF when peer 
requested to share art materials.

**BEHAVIOR DESCRIPTION:**
Wyatt exhibited Brief withdrawal characterized by:
- Loud vocal tone stating "No, mine!"
- Crossing arms and turning away
- Refusing to make eye contact with staff
- Duration: 3 minutes
- Intensity: Mild (Level 1 on BSP scale)

**INTERVENTION APPLIED:**
Staff Sebastian Cruz implemented:
1. Pause and proximity
2. Visual first-then board presentation
3. Choice offering between sharing materials or selecting different activity

Wyatt responded to choice offering intervention and returned to baseline within 
5 minutes.

**CONSEQUENCE:**
Brief access to preferred activity delayed by 2 minutes per Behavior Support Plan, followed by 
praise for appropriate choice-making.

**POST-INCIDENT:**
Wyatt participated in cooperative art activity with appropriate sharing behaviors 
observed. No further incidents during remainder of session.

**FUNCTIONAL COMMUNICATION:**
Wyatt was able to verbally request "my turn please" following de-escalation, 
demonstrating understanding of replacement behavior.

**PARENT NOTIFICATION:**
Phone contact with Justin Brooks at (315)432-5678. 
Parent reported similar sharing difficulties at home with sibling. Discussed consistency in 
intervention approach across settings.

**FOLLOW-UP ACTIONS:**
- Data entered into tracking system by Sebastian Cruz
- No modifications to current BSP recommended at this time
- Continue monitoring for pattern development

**Next session:** 04/22/2026 at 92 Geiger ICF
**Provider check-in:** Dr. Wilson on 5/04/2026

**Report filed by:** Sebastian Cruz
**Filed:** 10/10/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE

**Client:** J. Gray

**Time:** 10:00 AM - 11:00 AM
**Behavior Specialist:** Daniel Richardson

---

## SKILL ACQUISITION SESSION

**Target Skill:** Multi-step vocational task completion
**Teaching Method:** Discrete trial training with naturalistic teaching

**SESSION SUMMARY:**
James participated in 45 discrete trial training sessions focusing on lunch service 
preparation skills at Baldwinsville TEC. Session began at 10:00 AM with 
hand washing and apron donning.

**TRIAL DATA:**
- Trial block 1: 71% accuracy across 15 trials
- Trial block 2: 80% accuracy across 15 trials  
- Trial block 3: 91% accuracy across 15 trials
- Overall session accuracy: 88%

**PROMPTING HIERARCHY:**
Initial trials required full physical prompting, progressing to verbal prompting only by session end. 
James demonstrated improvement in response latency from 8.5 seconds to 3.2 seconds.

**VOCATIONAL INTEGRATION:**
James practiced food service skills during lunch preparation. Staff Avery Myers, MSW supervised and reported successful completion of assigned tasks with minimal support.

**PARENT COLLABORATION:**
Contacted Sharon Gray at 315-494-3456 to discuss home practice strategies. 
Parent reported James has been practicing sorting tasks at home with good success.

**NEXT SESSION GOALS:**
- Increase trial complexity for vocational skills
- Reduce prompting to gestural level only
- Incorporate generalization setting

**Therapist:** Daniel Richardson
**Date signed:** 11/11/2025

---
END OF SESSION NOTE
